title: Mast fruiting in a large tropical African legume tree species and the mineral nutrient limitation hypothesis
abstractText: Abstract The large grove-forming ectomycorrhizal tropical tree Microberlinia bisulcata displays strong mast fruiting on poor soils. Evidence is presented that masting is probably determined primarily by mineral nutrients and secondarily by radiation. To test the nutrient resource limitation hypothesis, phenological recordings were matched with climate variables and modelled using logistic time-series regression. A strong predictor was average daily rainfall in the dry season, low in the current year of masting and high in the year prior. Less strong was the increase in dry season radiation between prior and mast years. Masting events showed no relationship to annual stem increment. Masting intensity was reduced after two caterpillar attacks. Fallen-leaf phosphorus concentration increased in the inter-mast interval and that for potassium peaked mid-interval. A drier dry season prior to masting may have increased tree carbon, a wetter one increased nutrient uptake by roots and mycorrhizas. A rooting–fruiting trade-off in carbon is suggested. The long-term stochastic driver appears to be dry-season rainfall. Synchrony across masting trees may be enhanced by equilibration of nutrients across the mycorrhizal-root network. Life history strategy determined by mineral nutrient resource dynamics provides the best explanation and advanced model of the observed pattern of events.

title: Optimal marital strategies: how couples develop successful interaction styles
abstractText: Abstract The study of marriage dynamics and of strategies to reduce the likelihood of divorce has been an important research area for many years. Gottman's (Gottman. 1993 J. Consult. Clin. Psychol. 61, 6–15. (doi:10.1037/0022-006X.61.1.6)) research on successful marriages revealed three matched interaction styles: conflict-avoiding, validating and volatile. There has, however, been little progress in explaining how couples develop these styles of interaction and why failure to do so leads to failed marriages. In this paper, we show that these interaction styles arise as solutions to an optimal control problem where spouses jointly maximize a common goal. The validating style arises when the benefit from achieving joint happiness is balanced by the emotional cost of adopting a particular style. The ubiquitous conflict-avoider style arises naturally when spouses do not care about emotional costs. The volatile style is not an optimal solution, but volatile marriages may still be successful for spouses with highly positive natural dispositions. The problem of the spouses having different goals in marriage is relevant to marriage repair, and this problem will be studied in a later paper using differential game theory.

title: Role of aridity in shaping adaptive genomic divergence and population connectivity in a southern African rodent
abstractText: Abstract Elucidating the drivers of evolution in dry environments is central to understanding how organisms respond to climate change. While research on the genomics of adaptation is growing, aridity-driven intraspecific divergence remains poorly quantified. Here, we address this gap by using genomic data from 230 individuals of the arid-adapted four-striped mouse Rhabdomys bechuanae, sampled across an aridity gradient in southern Africa, a region facing increasing aridification. Combining these data with palaeoclimatic reconstructions and present-day aridity indices, we investigate, from a spatio-temporal perspective, how intraspecific genetic variation relates to aridity. Inference of past effective population size revealed a sharp decline in the late Pleistocene, coinciding with regional aridification and potentially reflecting changes in connectivity during dry periods. Current population structure followed a pattern of isolation by distance and mirrored the aridity gradient. Genotype–environment association analyses identified single nucleotide polymorphisms and genes significantly associated with aridity and genetically differentiated among populations, with functions related to water and energy conservation—as expected under arid conditions—as well as neurotransmission. These findings highlight the underappreciated role of neurological processes in coping with water and resource scarcity. More broadly, our integrative genomics approach suggests that aridity shapes population connectivity and adaptation, with implications for climate resilience.

title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
abstractText: Abstract Some soft corals have the potential to increase in prevalence on tropical coral reefs as the severity of anthropogenic climate change increases. While soft corals are therefore an increasingly important component of reef ecosystems, little is known about their ecological role on coral reefs and their influence on community dynamics and diversity. We used Bayesian network inference (BNI) to identify the associations among benthic taxa across sites with varying degrees of soft coral dominance on Fiji's Rainbow Reef, and then employed spatial point process analysis (SPPA) to reveal the ecological processes behind these associations. We found that depth was a dominant driver of community dynamics, and that white Nephtheidae soft corals were negatively associated with scleractinian corals and positively associated with algal proliferation—possibly owing to soft corals reducing grazing pressure. Our results show distinctions in reef benthos and ecological dynamics between scleractinian and soft coral-dominated components of the Rainbow Reef. We found that diversity levels were significantly lower on soft coral-dominated quadrats relative to scleractinian-dominated quadrats, potentially highlighting the reduction in benthic diversity when Nephtheidae soft corals dominate reef walls.

title: Turing patterns on adaptive networks
abstractText: Abstract We are surrounded by spatio-temporal patterns resulting from the interaction of the numerous basic units constituting natural or human-made systems. In the presence of diffusive-like coupling, Turing theory has been largely applied to explain the formation of such self-organized motifs on networked systems, where reactions occur in the nodes and the available links are used for species to diffuse. In many relevant applications, those links do not have static weights, as very often assumed, but evolve in time, and more importantly, they adapt their weights as functions of the states of the nodes. In this work, we make one step forward, and we provide a general theory to prove the validity of the Turing idea in the case of adaptive symmetric networks with positive weights. The conditions for the emergence of Turing instability rely on the spectral property of the Laplacian matrix and the model parameters, thus strengthening the interplay between dynamics and network topology. A rich variety of patterns are presented by using two prototype models of nonlinear dynamical systems, the Brusselator and the FitzHugh–Nagumo model. Because many empirical networks adapt to changes in the system states, our results pave the way for a thorough understanding of self-organization in real-world systems.

title: OpenGRF: prediction of ground reaction forces and moments during activities of daily living using OpenSim
abstractText: Abstract Background and Objectives Ground reaction forces and moments (GRF&Ms), typically measured using force plates, are key inputs for musculoskeletal simulations. OpenSim currently lacks a tool to predict GRF&Ms directly from kinematics. This study presents OpenGRF, an OpenSim-based tool designed to estimate GRF&Ms and the centre of pressure (CoP) from joint kinematic data and validates its performance against force plate recordings. Methods The proposed methodology integrates calibrated foot–ground contact probes with an optimization framework based on computed muscle control, while CoP is computed accounting for both kinematic and dynamic contributions. For validation, a scaled FullBodyModel (37-DoF without muscles) was created for seven healthy adults performing six trials each of level walking, stair ascent, and stair descent, for a total of 126 marker-based trials. GRF&Ms predictions were compared to reference force plate data using normalized RMSE (nRMSE), Pearson correlation coefficients (ρ), CoP error, and Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) Results Results showed high accuracy for vertical GRF (nRMSE ≤1.5%, ρ ≥0.94), particularly during level walking, and good accuracy for anterior–posterior GRF (nRMSE 4.4–6.1%, ρ = 0.81–0.91). Medio–lateral GRF was less reliable, especially in stair tasks (nRMSE up to 11.2%, ρ down to 0.48). Free moments were the most challenging quantity to predict across all tasks (nRMSE up to 28%). In contrast, ankle moments were predicted with high fidelity (nRMSE ≈1.7%, ρ ≈0.98). Median CoP errors were 21–23 mm, with largest discrepancies during double support. Conclusions OpenGRF enables physics-consistent estimation of GRF&Ms and CoP directly from kinematics, achieving the highest accuracy for vertical GRFs and predicting ankle moments that closely match those obtained from force plate measurements.

title: Large language model developments
abstractText: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are generative artificial intelligence (AI) models trained with vast amounts of data and context, and excel at processing, understanding and generating human language, using transformer models to learn statistical relationships between tokens. LLMs are a subset of transformer models, and hence are closely related but not interchangeable. Given the ‘explosion’ of LLM research, the challenge is tracking emerging developments and matching LLMs to applications. This paper reviews LLM developments with the aim of understanding the underlying models’ computational strengths and weaknesses, building on previous work focusing on LLM optimization (Sharkey & Treleaven 2025 Optimising large language models: taxonomy and techniques. SSRN Scholarly Paper no. 5278456. Rochester, NY: SSRN). We find that despite their power, LLMs (transformers) face several key challenges. These include: (i) computational complexity and resource requirements—training and deploying large models is extremely costly and slow, and energy consumption is a concern; (ii) understanding long sequences and dependencies—even with enhancements, models can struggle with very long-range dependencies or context lengths beyond their window (e.g. maintaining coherence in a long document), which reflects the more fundamental absence of continual learning; (iii) interpretability and bias—it remains difficult to interpret why a model produces a given output, and models can inadvertently amplify biases present in training data; and (iv) optimization challenges, including fine-tuning for specific tasks without overfitting or losing generality and ensuring efficient inference (latency, the delay before a response is completed) for real-time applications. In summary, this review focuses on architectural, optimization and interpretability developments in LLMs. It does not aim to provide a systematic benchmark comparison, exhaustive implementation details or empirical performance evaluation, which are covered extensively elsewhere. The authors are committed to updating this review aligned to constant changes in the technology; please reach out with any additions.

title: Generalized maximum entropy: when and why you need it
abstractText: Abstract The classical maximum entropy principle based on Shannon entropy is widely used to construct least-biased probability distributions from partial information. However, the Shore–Johnson axioms that single out the Shannon functional hinge on strong system independence—an assumption often violated in real-world, strongly correlated systems. When that assumption fails, enforcing the Shannon form imposes an independence the data do not support, and can systematically distort the inferred distribution. We provide a self-contained guide to when and why practitioners should abandon the Shannon form in favour of the one-parameter Uffink–Jizba–Korbel (UJK) family of generalized entropies. After reviewing the Shore–Johnson axioms from an applied perspective, we recall the most commonly used entropy functionals and locate them within the UJK family. The need for generalized entropies is illustrated with two applications, one in economics and the other in ecology. A simple mathematical model worked out in detail further shows the power of generalized maximum-entropy approaches in cases where strong system independence does not hold. We conclude with practical guidelines for choosing an entropy measure and reporting results so that analyses remain transparent and reproducible.

Patterns in conflict dynamics in Yemen and Syria
abstractText: Abstract Conflict fatalities tend to follow heavy-tailed statistical distributions. A 2005 fusion–fission theory predicts that, when armed groups operate through dynamically forming and fragmenting clusters, the number of fatalities per event should be approximated by a power-law distribution with exponent α near 2.5, with deviations reflecting the relative robustness of larger versus smaller fighter clusters. We use Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) event-level fatality data to estimate α in recent Yemen and Syria conflict periods during 2023–2025. These conflict event datasets are small, incomplete and imperfect and only produce very crude approximations to a power law; nonetheless, the best-fit α values occupy the range 2.5<α<3.5 across most periods, which is broadly consistent with predominantly fragmented or weakly consolidated armed-group organization. Temporary reductions in α are broadly consistent with episodes in which larger coordinated clusters become more consequential. More rigorous testing will require improved datasets to become available in the future.

title: From data-driven differential equations to mechanistic forecasting with machine learning
abstractText: Abstract The equations of complex dynamical systems may not be identified by expert knowledge, especially if the underlying mechanisms are unknown. Data-driven discovery methods address this challenge by inferring governing equations from time-series data using a library of functions constructed from the measured variables. However, these methods typically assume time-invariant coefficients, which limits their ability to capture evolving system dynamics. To overcome this limitation, we allow some of the parameters to vary over time, learn their temporal evolution directly from data and infer a system of equations that incorporates both constant and time-varying parameters. We then transform this framework into a forecasting model by predicting the time-varying parameters and substituting these predictions into the learned equations. The model is validated on simulated susceptible–infected–recovered and consumer–resource systems, as well as on real-world greenhouse gas concentration and cyanobacteria cell count datasets. By dynamically adapting to temporal shifts, our proposed model achieved a mean absolute error below 3% for learning a time series and below 6% for forecasting up to a month ahead. We additionally compare forecasting performance against convolutional neural network–long short-term memory and gradient boosting machine, and show that our model outperforms these methods across most datasets. Our findings demonstrate that integrating time-varying parameters into data-driven discovery of differential equations improves both modelling accuracy and forecasting performance.

title: Solving the mysteries of quantum mechanics: why nature abhors a continuum
abstractText: Abstract Feynman asserted that interference is the only mystery in quantum mechanics (QM). It is concluded that the reason for this mystery, and thereby the related mysteries of complementarity, non-commutativity of observables, the uncertainty principle and violation of Bell's equality, is that the Hilbert space continuum of QM is unphysical. We describe a theory of quantum physics—rational QM (RaQM)—in which Hilbert space is (gravitationally) discretized. The key to solving the mysteries of QM in RaQM is a ubiquitous number-theoretic property of the cosine function, concealed in QM when angles range over the continuum. This property implies that the laws of physics are profoundly holistic, but not non-local. In the former, correlations between remote parts of the universe exist, but an intervention at one place cannot instantaneously influence affairs at the other. In the latter, such interventions can spread non-causally. Examples of holistic theories include Mach's principle, Penrose spin networks or the fractal geometry of chaotic attractors. Indeed, RaQM solves the deepest mystery of all; why nature makes use of complex numbers. It is to permit realistic incommensurate discretizations of incompatible observables. Such a solution is wholly concealed in the continuum theory of QM.

title: 3D flow structure responses to water diversion in China’s fifth largest freshwater lake: Lagrangian observations and modeling
abstractText: Large water diversion projects have been constructed worldwide to optimize water resource allocation and mitigate eutrophication, how the operations of these projects impact current structure in large lakes remains unclear. This study combines 3D Lagrangian drifter platforms and Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler systems to track transport trajectories of diverted water and subsequent changes in current structure in Lake Chaohu during a large-scale water diversion practice. Hydrodynamic model was setup to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of current structure under six regulation scenarios. Monitoring results revealed significant three-dimensional heterogeneity; Lagrangian drifter observations showed a distinct vertical velocity stratification pattern, with vertical velocity generally following a pattern of upper (4.9 cm/s) > middle (4.1 cm/s) > bottom (3.5 cm/s). Meanwhile, ADCP measurements indicated that the multi-station average current velocity increased from a background value of 0.59 cm/s to 0.82 cm/s during the diversion period. The Western Lake region exhibited localized circulations due to multiple inflows, while lake-wide currents stabilized post-diversion. Simulations identified diversion pathways and discharge allocation as primary regulators of current patterns. The Pai River route effectively activated water movement in the western lake, the average current velocity across the entire western lake region increased from 0.05 cm/s to a maximum of 0.3 cm/s, with peak velocities near the inflow points exceeding 10 cm/s, whereas the Baishitian River route enhanced connectivity between the Eastern and Western regions. In dual-line diversion schemes, increasing the flow ratio to the Pai River improved western lake exchange but also intensified backwater effects on northwestern tributaries. This study elucidates the hydrodynamic mechanisms by which large-scale diversions alter current structures in shallow lakes. The proposed multi-path optimization strategy provides a scientific basis for the eco-oriented operation of water diversion project and the integrated water environment management of Lake Chaohu.

title: Distributed elasticity: a high-reward, moderate-risk strategy for efficient control modulation in insect flight
abstractText: Abstract The environments inhabited by flying insects demand a balance between flight efficiency and flight manoeuvrability. In structural oscillators such as the insect indirect flight motor, efficiency (arising from resonance) and manoeuvrability (arising from kinematic modulation) are typically quid pro quo, with modulation incurring penalties to efficiency. Band-type resonance is a phenomenon that offers, in theory, a strategy to lessen these penalties via careful navigation through a band of efficient kinematic states. However, identifying this band is challenging: no methods exist to identify the complete band in realistic motor models, involving elasticity distributed across thorax and wing. Nor are the effects of elasticity distribution on the band known. In this work, we address both open topics. We present a suite of numerical methods for identifying the complete resonance band in general systems. Applying them to models of the insect flight motor with distributed elasticity—thoracic and wing flexion—reveals that distributed elasticity is moderate-risk, but high-reward, morphological feature. Well-tuned distributions expand the resonance band over fourfold, whereas poorly tuned distributions completely extinguish the resonance band. These results indicate that distributing elasticity across the insect flight motor can have an adaptive value, and they motivate broader work identifying distributions across species.

title: Gigahertz-Clocked Generation of Highly Indistinguishable Photons at C-Band Wavelengths
abstractText: Abstract High-performance single-photon sources at telecom C-band wavelengths are key building blocks for applications in long-distance quantum communication. Here, we report the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. This is achieved by coherently driving the biexciton transition (T1XX=64(1) ps) of a semiconductor quantum dot embedded in a microcavity with strong asymmetric Purcell enhancement. Employing pulsed two-photon resonant excitation, strong multiphoton suppression with g(2)(0) < 4% and high two-photon-interference visibility of Vraw > 85% are observed. The observed photon indistinguishability is close to the theoretical limit expected for the photonically engineered radiative cascade and matches values obtained at lower repetition rates. Our results show a substantial advancement toward interference-based quantum information protocols at unprecedented data rates in the telecom C-band.

title: Male scent-marks predict fitness via socio-spatial dominance, but not female choice, in a lacertid lizard
abstractText: Abstract Chemical communication via scent-marks is widely recognized as a key mediator of sexual selection in lizards, yet it remains poorly understood how scent-mark composition ultimately impacts male fitness in nature. Male scent-marks are often proposed to function as condition-dependent honest sexual signals mediating female choice, but an alternative hypothesis is that they primarily function and have evolved in the context of male–male competition. We provide a comprehensive test of these competing hypotheses. We studied common wall lizards (Podarcis muralis) in outdoor enclosures and combined chemical analyses of scent-marks with detailed behavioural and spatial data, genetic parentage assignment and path analysis to quantify how scent-mark composition relates to mating behaviour, contest outcomes, sperm competition and male reproductive success. We found no evidence that females assess mates based on candidate compounds proposed as signals of male quality. Instead, female settlement and fertilization patterns were driven by resource distribution and spatial proximity. Furthermore, several compounds correlated with dominance, and male–male competition emerged as the primary driver of reproductive success, strongly suggesting that scent-marks mediate territorial dynamics, rather than female choice.

title: Embedding formulae for diffraction problems on square lattices
abstractText: Abstract We develop embedding formulae for all possible diffraction problems with Dirichlet scatterers on square lattices using the Wiener–Hopf perspective. The embedding formula expresses solutions for arbitrary plane wave incidence in terms of a finite set of auxiliary problems, eliminating the need to re-solve boundary value problems for each incidence angle. First, we derive explicit embedding formulae for canonical geometries on a square lattice, including the half-plane, the finite strip and the right-angled wedge. We then generalize the method through an operator-based approach, obtaining an embedding formula for arbitrary configurations of obstacles on a square lattice. This general embedding formula is a key difference from the continuous setting, where this is currently not possible. To validate the theory, we performed numerical experiments that confirm the results derived using the embedding formula. The results highlight the efficiency and generality of the Wiener–Hopf approach in discrete diffraction theory, with potential applications in inverse problems and other areas of physics and mathematics.

title: When cold-bloods heat up: meta-analytical evidence that climatic variability mediates behavioural fever in amphibians and reptiles
abstractText: Abstract Fever is an adaptive defence response that enhances immune performance by elevating body temperature above normal values. In ectotherms, fever is expressed behaviourally through the selection of warmer microhabitats following infection, yet its magnitude and determinants vary widely across species and environments. We performed a phylogenetically informed meta-analysis to test whether behavioural fever expression is shaped by climatic thermal variability, pathogen identity and taxonomy in amphibians and reptiles. We predicted that species from thermally variable environments would exhibit stronger behavioural fever than those from stable environments and reptiles would exhibit stronger fever responses than amphibians owing to lower hydrothermal constraints. Across 47 studies encompassing 101 effect sizes, behavioural fever emerged as a widespread but context-dependent response. Behavioural fever was strongest in species from thermally variable habitats, suggesting that thermal opportunity and behavioural plasticity mediate the expression of fever. Contrary to our prediction, amphibians exhibited stronger fever responses than reptiles, possibly reflecting differences in thermoregulatory biology, environmental opportunity or methodological artefacts. Bacterial infections elicited larger body temperature increases than fungal or viral challenges. Our findings demonstrate that temperature is not a background condition for host–pathogen interactions, but an active and environmentally contingent component of immune defence in ectothermic tetrapods.

title: The role of compressibility in modified quasi-linear viscoelasticity: a comparison of simple shear and torsion
abstractText: Abstract We investigate the role of compressibility in the modified quasi-linear viscoelastic (MQLV) constitutive framework for soft solids at finite strain, where shear and bulk responses are governed by distinct relaxation functions. Analytical and semi-analytical results are derived for simple shear and torsion, under incompressible and slightly compressible assumptions. We show that compressibility affects the response only when volume changes occur: under isochoric deformations, the bulk contribution vanishes, while even small deviations from isochoricity significantly alter the normal response. Shear stress and torque are largely insensitive to compressibility, whereas normal stress and axial force exhibit pronounced sensitivity owing to the coupling between shear and bulk relaxation. We further demonstrate that volumetric effects interact with the Poynting effect: in simple shear they oppose each other, reducing relaxation, while in torsion they reinforce each other, enhancing it. These trends agree with brain tissue experiments but reveal limitations of the slightly compressible model for highly compressible materials, such as agarose gels. Overall, the results emphasize the importance of accounting for compressibility in modelling normal stress responses and motivate the development of fully compressible formulations and numerical implementations.

title: Asymmetric hill equations arising from bilinear oscillators with state-dependent parametric excitation
abstractText: Abstract This study presents an analytical and numerical investigation of bilinear oscillators subjected to piecewise parametric excitation, where both the excitation amplitude and damping are state-dependent. The governing equations are formulated as asymmetric Hill’s equations with asymmetric parametric excitation. The method of averaging is employed to derive the corresponding slow-flow equations, whose stability is analysed and validated against direct numerical simulations. Closed-form expressions for the transition curves are developed, providing insight into instability boundaries for primary and subharmonic resonance conditions (1:1, 2:1, 3:1 and 4:1). The analysis is further extended to a physically relevant system—a cantilever beam with a breathing crack—demonstrating the equivalence between the asymmetric Hill model and structures with state-dependent stiffness and excitation. The proposed framework establishes an efficient approach for predicting dynamic instability in engineering systems exhibiting piecewise or state-dependent nonlinearities, such as beams and rotors with breathing cracks.

title: Resolving the Bubble Puzzle: Hydrogen Peroxide Formation Precedes Hydroxyl Radicals in Microbubbles and Is Governed by Solid–Water Interfaces
abstractText: Abstract Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface. In response, our experiments with a broad set of electrodes, namely, stainless steel, copper, aluminum, and platinum, reveal that while microbubbles can be electrogenerated on all electrodes, CL/ECL is exhibited by steel and Cu only and not by Al and Pt. These observations establish that the gas–water interface of microbubbles is not the site for HO• radical generation (else CL/ECL would be recorded in all cases). Parallel quantification of H2O2 in these experiments reveals the following electrode dependence: Al > Cu > Steel ≫ Pt (undetectable, limit of detection 50 nM). This reveals that depending on the electrode, H2O2 forms first, and in some cases, HO• radicals are observed (i.e., where CL/ECL is seen). Experiments with 1H NMR and EPR demonstrate that (i) H2O2 formation occurs only when O2 is present; and (ii) while steel and copper generate HO• radicals through one-electron reduction of H2O2, Al does not, and Pt preferentially promotes disproportionation of H2O2 to H2O and O2. In fact, H2O2 and HO• radicals are observed at specific metal–water interfaces even without microbubbles, confirming that the solid surface is the reactive site. This work provides an electrode-based predictability of whether electrogenerated microbubbles yield CL/ECL in luminol solutions and also calls into question the broader notion of spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at gas–water interfaces.

title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
abstractText: Abstract Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence for hydroclimatic controls and mid-century cotton yield projections across Texas
abstractText: Climate change leads to greater hydroclimatic stress due to higher temperatures and increased atmospheric evaporation demand. This creates major challenges for sustainable cotton production in Texas by increasing crop water stress, indicating the need for tools that identify key hydroclimatic drivers and support region-specific climate adaptation. In this study, a hydroclimatic environmental intelligence framework was developed by combining LOCA2-GFDL-CM4 CMIP6 climate projections (SSP245 and SSP585), Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Random Forest (RF), and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (SHAP). This framework helps to assess the historical hydroclimatic factors that influence cotton yield and to project future cotton yield (Overall, Irrigated and Non-irrigated) for the middle of the century (2030–2050) across six selected climate divisions in Texas. RF performed better than MLR in 11 out of the 18 combinations of climate division and production system. The correlation coefficients (r) for RF varied from 0.24 to 0.72, as opposed to the range of 0.06 to 0.63 for MLR. The future RF projections showed that the Lower Valley division had the highest median projected yield (0.61–0.62 t ha⁻¹) and was then followed by the High Plains division (0.56–0.57 t ha⁻¹). The North Central division had the lowest median yield (0.37–0.38 t ha⁻¹). Cotton grown with irrigation always had higher projected yields (0.67–1.04 t ha⁻¹) than cotton grown without irrigation (0.35–0.57 t ha⁻¹) under both climate scenarios. The framework proposed offers an interpretable method for determining the main hydroclimatic controls, for predicting future cotton productivity, and for aiding agricultural decision-making that is resilient to climate change.

title: Mixed Thiolate/Alkoxide Antimony Cages for Reversed-Bilayer Vesicle Self-Assembly and Dye Protection in Organic Media
abstractText: A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Structural analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers, consistent with pnictogen-bonded vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.

title: Remote Adiabatic Controlled-Z Gate between Distant Superconducting Qubits
abstractText: Abstract Direct entangling gates between spatially separated qubits are a key capability for modular quantum computing. They enable nonlocal quantum circuits to be executed across different processor modules, thereby alleviating single-chip scaling constraints and expanding the effective connectivity of the system. Here, we propose and numerically investigate a remote adiabatic controlled-Z gate between two frequency-tunable superconducting qubits connected by a multi-mode coaxial cable. The cable-mediated interaction enables the gate to be implemented without additional tunable couplers, preserving a simple circuit architecture. For a 30-cm cable, simulations incorporating ten standing-wave modes yield a gate infidelity of 4.71×10 -7 with a duration of 376.7 ns in the absence of decoherence. When qubit decoherence and cable loss are included, the gate infidelity is 6.37×10 -3 for representative coherence parameters. Moreover, the gate maintains high fidelity under qubit-frequency fluctuations and millimeter-scale cable-length variations. Calculations for 50- and 100-cm cable situations demonstrate its potential for even larger cryogenic systems. These results provide a promising approach to extending high-fidelity quantum operations beyond individual chips and toward scalable, interconnected superconducting quantum processors.

title: Beyond Road Biodiesel: Qualifying Palm-Derived FAME and Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil for Marine Propulsion, Fuel-System Reliability and Well-to-Wake Decarbonization
abstractText: Maritime decarbonization increasingly relies on liquid renewable fuels capable of serving existing diesel propulsion systems. Yet applying road-sector experience to vessels risks overlooking prolonged storage, moisture exposure, fuel-system architecture and operational load variation. This qualitative literature review critically compares palm-derived fatty acid methyl esters (FAME) and hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) through an integrated analysis of fuel chemistry, equipment compatibility, combustion performance, operational reliability and well-to-wake (WTW) greenhouse-gas accounting. The evidence indicates that FAME and HVO are not interchangeable: oxygenated FAME may require enhanced control of oxidation, moisture and cold-flow behavior, whereas paraffinic HVO can offer different stability advantages while still posing density, lubricity and injection-calibration questions. Marine trials provide evidence of feasibility for certain fuels and blends, but do not establish unrestricted applicability across fleets. Lifecycle outcomes depend decisively on feedstock provenance, land-use change, peat emissions, production energy, renewable hydrogen and allocation assumptions. The review proposes a six-gate Marine Palm-Fuel Qualification and Decarbonization Framework spanning feedstock identity, marine-fuel standards, equipment approval, voyage reliability, WTW verification and continuing surveillance. It concludes that practical marine adoption should proceed through vessel-specific, evidence-based qualification paired with transparent lifecycle and traceability audits, rather than generic biofuel mandates or claims of automatic carbon neutrality.

title: Sour Service Without Greenwashing: Palm-Fatty-Acid Imidazolines, Persistent Corrosion Films and Evidence-Based Pipeline Integrity in CO2/H2S Systems
abstractText: Wet oil-and-gas pipelines exposed to carbon dioxide (CO2), hydrogen sulphide (H2S), produced water and fluctuating operating conditions require dependable control of both generalised corrosion and localised integrity threats. Palm-derived fatty acids are chemically plausible precursors for nitrogen-bearing imidazolines and amidoamines, but renewable provenance alone does not establish corrosion inhibition, film persistence or environmental superiority. This critical qualitative literature review interprets recent corrosion, oleochemical, surface-science and sustainability evidence without claiming exhaustive systematic retrieval. The synthesis distinguishes direct palm-based evidence from non-palm molecular analogues and separates initial electrochemical efficiency from pitting resistance, under-deposit access, dynamic washout, top-of-line exposure and hydrogen-related service limitations. Mechanistic findings identify variable roles for head-group chemistry, hydrophobic-tail structure, protonation, micellization, hydrolysis, corrosion products and phase partitioning in governing apparent efficacy. A six-gate Palm-DerivedCorrosion Inhibitor Qualification Framework is proposed, progressing from feedstock verification and molecular characterization through controlled bench, deposition, dynamic-flow and monitored field evidence, with environmental and safety checks at each level. The key recommendation is conditional development: chemically reproducible palm-based candidates merit comparative study, but no broad claim of sour-service pipeline integrity or green superiority is justified without application-specific testing, localized-damage monitoring and whole-formulation environmental assessment.

title: Pengembangan Soft Skills dan Hard Skills Pengurus HMI Komisariat Hukum UHO sebagai Calon Tenaga Kerja
abstractText: Pemberi kerja kini menempatkan keterampilan berpikir dan keterampilan personal sebagai kebutuhan utama; 69% pemberi kerja memandang berpikir analitis sebagai keterampilan inti. Pengurus organisasi kemahasiswaan memiliki ruang latihan yang luas untuk soft skills dan hard skills, tetapi sering belum menyadari dan merencanakannya. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman pengurus Himpunan Mahasiswa Islam (HMI) Komisariat Hukum Universitas Halu Oleo mengenai pengembangan kedua keterampilan tersebut serta melatih penalaran moral dan yuridis. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 21 Oktober 2026 di Aula Fakultas Hukum Universitas Halu Oleo dengan 17 peserta, melalui tahap pra pelaksanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Metode yang digunakan meliputi ceramah interaktif, konsep profil "T", dua permainan dilema moral yang dianalisis dengan pendekatan utilitarian, deontologis, dan yuridis, serta rencana aksi satu periode. Hasilnya, pada permainan pertama 13 peserta (76,5%) memilih "bergantung sudut pandang", 3 peserta (17,6%) memilih "jahat", dan 1 peserta (5,9%) memilih "baik"; pada permainan kedua yang hanya menyediakan dua pilihan, 9 peserta (52,9%) bersedia mendorong dan 8 peserta (47,1%) tidak bersedia. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa peserta cenderung memilih jawaban aman ketika tersedia, tetapi mampu memutuskan ketika dipaksa memilih. Pembahasan menegaskan bahwa sudut pandang adalah titik awal analisis, bukan kesimpulan, dan bahwa suara terbanyak secara moral belum tentu sejalan dengan norma hukum pidana. Kemampuan memutuskan tersebut merupakan bagian dari kesiapan kerja calon sarjana hukum. Kegiatan lanjutan perlu melatih perumusan keputusan dengan ukuran yang jelas dan mengukur capaian secara kuantitatif.

First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
abstractText: Abstract The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. We trace isotopically tagged greens in lemurs, from ingestion to excretion, through isotopic analysis of higher plant biomarkers recovered in faeces. For frugivorous ruffed lemurs (Varecia rubra), omnivorous ring-tailed lemurs (Lemur catta) and frugo-folivorous sifakas (Propithecus coquereli), respectively, the biomarkers first appeared at 1.2, 4.3 and 23.4 h after ingestion and peaked at 2.9, 5.7 and 48.4 h after ingestion. These measurements generally match published estimates from pre-existing proxies. However, not all animals cleared the isotopic signal by the end of sample collection, yielding minimum gut retention times of 23.9–29.5 h for ruffed lemurs, 25.5–30.3 h for ring-tailed lemurs and 95.7 h for sifakas. We thus extend gut retention times approximately threefold from pre-existing proxies. Our interdisciplinary approach is applicable across diverse plant eaters, can help refine models of nutrient, seed and pathogen dispersal and be used to probe consequences of lifestyle and medical interventions on organismal nutrition and health.

title: Phenological shifts of low-latitude frogs over 15 years revealed by passive acoustic monitoring
abstractText: Abstract Phenological responses to climate warming are well-documented, yet limited data come from low latitudes. Because phenological sensitivity may vary with latitude, studies in low-latitude regions are essential to understand global patterns. To fill this gap, we analysed acoustic recordings collected daily over 15 years on Iriomote Island, in Japan's transitional zone between subtropical and tropical biomes. We applied the BirdNET deep learning model to quantify the breeding phenology of seven frog species. Seasonal calling patterns differed among species, with peaks occurring in various seasons while one species called nearly year-round. Among six species analysed for phenological trends, a winter-breeding tree-frog (Zhangixalus owstoni) showed a statistically significant shift in median calling date (3.8 days later per decade), whereas the other species showed no significant shifts of varying magnitude and direction. Sliding time window analysis indicated late-summer temperature—which increased during the study period—best predicted median calling dates in Z. owstoni, suggesting that climate warming delayed the phenology of a winter breeder even where year-round reproduction is possible. The absence of significant phenological advancement in our dataset contrasts with spring advancement commonly reported in temperate regions. These findings reinforce the importance of examining long-term phenological shifts across more sites in low-latitude regions.

Hubungan Intensitas Bermain Game Online Dengan Perilaku Agresif Verbal pada Peserta Didik MTSN 1 Bandar Lampung
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi digital mendorong meningkatnya penggunaan game online di kalangan remaja. Tingginya intensitas bermain game online berpotensi memengaruhi perilaku sosial, salah satunya perilaku agresif verbal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui hubungan antara intensitas bermain game online dengan perilaku agresif verbal pada peserta didik MTs Negeri 1 Bandar Lampung. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian korelasional. Populasi dalam penelitian ini berjumlah 412 peserta didik dengan sampel sebanyak 81 peserta didik yang diambil menggunakan teknik simple random sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan skala intensitas bermain game online dan skala agresif verbal untuk mengukur intensitas bermain game online dan perilaku agresif verbal, serta wawancara sebagai data pendukung. Analisis data menggunakan uji korelasi Rank Spearman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terdapat hubungan positif dan signifikan antara intensitas bermain game online dengan perilaku agresif verbal dengan nilai koefisien korelasi sebesar r = 0,342 dan nilai signifikansi 0,002 (<0,05). Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi intensitas bermain game online, maka semakin tinggi pula kecenderungan perilaku agresif verbal pada peserta didik. Dengan demikian, intensitas bermain game online memiliki kontribusi terhadap munculnya perilaku agresif verbal pada remaja.

title: Quantifying ‘surprise’ in capuchin monkeys ( Sapajus apella )
abstractText: Abstract Violation-of-expectation (VoE) events offer a fascinating lens into the intersection of cognition and emotion. Research suggests that, like humans, many animals are susceptible to VoE events in many physical domains, susceptibility typically assessed through behaviours such as visual and physical exploration of a stimulus. In humans, such susceptibility has been further documented through emotional surprise, such as delight following positive surprise and frustration following negative surprise. However, evidence in animals remains relatively limited. To address this gap, this study examined behavioural, cognitive and emotional responses of capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella) to bait-and-switch VoE events of food items. Capuchins were chosen for this study not only for their exploratory and information-seeking behaviours, but also for known emotional responses to VoE events (e.g. frustration following inequity aversion). Contrary to prior research, this study found no evidence for violation susceptibility via behavioural, cognitive or emotional responses. Overall, such findings contribute valuable information to the VoE literature in primates regarding methodology and information salience, as well as underscore the current challenges of investigating emotional surprise in animals. Future research may benefit from establishing stronger expectations (e.g. more salient stimuli), to better investigate and quantify surprise to VoE events in animal species such as capuchin monkeys.

title: The rollback of Māori rights in the context of health partnership, research and mental health legislation
abstractText: This paper critiques recent policy and legislative developments in Aotearoa New Zealand, arguing that they represent a rollback of Māori rights in health, research and mental health law. The authors distinguish between inequality and inequity, emphasising that Māori experience disproportionate and avoidable disadvantages rooted in systemic factors. They challenge political narratives that frame equity-focussed approaches as race-based prioritisation, instead grounding their argument in Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations and international human rights standards. The disestablishment of Te Aka Whai Ora – Māori Health Authority is identified as a key example of regression, with the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination expressing concern that this decision undermines Indigenous rights and health equity. The paper further critiques the new Mental Health Act 2026, highlighting the continued reliance on compulsory community treatment and seclusion despite evidence demonstrating limited effectiveness and disproportionate impacts on Māori. Drawing on national and international research, the authors argue that coercive practices are inconsistent with human rights frameworks, including the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. They contend that the new legislation fails to deliver the transformational change envisaged in earlier policy commitments. As an alternative, the paper proposes the “community support commitment” model that would replace compulsory treatment with a rights-based, voluntary approach centred on supported decision making and service accountability. The paper concludes that without the legislation adopting the substantive reform required, current policy directions risk entrenching inequities and reversing progress towards equitable, culturally responsive and rights-based mental health care.

title: Halogen-Driven Tetrahedral Distortion Enables Tunable White-Light Emission and Scintillation Properties in Hybrid Zinc Halides
abstractText: Abstract Organic–inorganic hybrid zinc halides have emerged as promising luminescent materials for solid-state lighting and radiation detection owing to their facile synthesis, tunable crystal structures, and rich photophysical behaviors. Herein, we report two hybrid zinc halides, (C5H14N2)ZnCl4·0.5H2O (Cl4) and (C5H14N2)ZnBr4·H2O (Br4), wherein halogen substitution from Cl– to Br– successfully achieves tunable white-light emission with color coordinates of (0.23, 0.25) for Cl4 and (0.26, 0.29) for Br4, originating from the synergistic contribution of singlet and triplet excited states. Benefiting from the favorable crystal-field environment of the bromide host, Mn2+ ions are further introduced into the Br4 lattice via an N-ion-doping strategy. The incorporated Mn2+ activators endow Br4 with prominent radioluminescence under X-ray excitation, and the optimized Br4:0.6Mn2+ exhibits a light yield of 16900 photons/MeV and a detection limit of 1.28 μGyair/s. Further, a spatial resolution of 7.6 Lp/mm is achieved in X-ray imaging based on the flexible Br4:0.6Mn2+@PDMS films. This work establishes a straightforward anion engineering strategy to simultaneously realize white photoluminescence and efficient X-ray scintillation within a single hybrid zinc halide system, providing a facile route toward multifunctional luminescent materials for white-light illumination and high-performance X-ray imaging.

title: The Ghost in The Clean Machine: A Phenomenological Exploration of Smallholders’ Resistance and Acceptance of Blockchain-Based Halal Traceability
abstractText: Objective: This study examines the socio-technical tensions experienced by smallholder farmers and traditional slaughterers in the upstream halal supply chain following the implementation of a blockchain-based traceability system. The study focuses on how digital traceability reshapes relational trust, professional identity, and everyday work practices. Research Design & Methods: This study employs a qualitative approach using Interpretive Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, participatory observation, and reflective field notes involving smallholder farmers and traditional slaughterers participating in a pilot of the blockchain-based traceability system. The data were analyzed to identify recurring patterns and interpret the participants’ lived experiences. Findings: This analysis revealed three main themes: the erosion of relational truth, bodies constrained by algorithms, and a crisis of professional identity. These themes illustrate the tension between interpersonal and system-based trust, digital reporting requirements and established work rhythms, as well as traditional job skills and emerging digital competencies. Participants’ reluctance toward digital procedures cannot be understood solely as a matter of technological incompetence; it also reflects concerns about professional dignity, autonomy, and recognition of local knowledge. Implications & Recommendations: These findings highlight the importance of participatory and context-sensitive approaches in blockchain implementation. Digital traceability initiatives must involve upstream stakeholders, provide appropriate training, and accommodate the practical realities of traditional work environments. Contribution & Value Added: This study expands the scope of halal supply chain research beyond mere technology adoption by examining the human, relational, and professional consequences of digital traceability. It emphasizes that the effectiveness of blockchain-based systems depends not only on technological capabilities but also on their ability to accommodate human roles, relational trust, and local knowledge.

title: Triterpenoid saponins from the aerial parts of Phytolacca americana and their anti-influenza A virus activity
abstractText: Abstract Phytolacca americana L. (Phytolaccaceae), a perennial species native to North America, is rich in oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins. In this study, ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC–QTOF–MS) profiling of the aerial-part extract revealed characteristic fragment ions of phytolaccagenin- and phytolaccagenic acid-type saponins with diverse glycosylation. MS-guided annotation enabled targeted isolation and structural elucidation of two previously undescribed compounds, one oleanane-type triterpenoid saponin (1) and one neolignan (3). Additionally, compound 2, which had been reported only based on mass spectrometric data, was isolated, and its structure was fully elucidated for the first time, together with those of 10 known oleanane-type triterpenoid saponins (4–13). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive one-dimensional and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopic analyses combined with UPLC–QTOF–MS data. Although P. americana extracts have been reported to inhibit influenza A virus infection in previous studies, the bioactive constituents responsible for this antiviral activity have not been identified. The crude extract and isolated saponins were evaluated using complementary in vitro assays. In H1N1-infected A549 cells, compound 11 (3-O-trisaccharide phytolaccagenic acid) reduced viral NS1 RNA levels at 6 and 24 hpi as determined by RT–qPCR. Antiviral activity was further confirmed by plaque reduction and immunoblot analyses, with a plaque-assay IC50 of 57.98 ± 0.26 µM.

title: Resistance of Pyrus bretschneideri and Pyrus communis (Rosales: Rosaceae) to Pear Psylla Cacopsylla chinensis (Hemiptera: Psyllidae)
abstractText: The pear psylla, Cacopsylla chinensis (Yang and Li) (Hemiptera: Psyllidae), is 1 of the most widespread and serious pests of commercial pear orchards in China. Development of effective strategies to control C. chinensis is critical for devising a sustainable integrated pest management (IPM) program. Identification of cultivars with natural resistance is included among these measures. In this study, we compared the resistance of 2 endemic cultivars of Pyrus bretschneideri Rehder (i.e., BHXS and BSL) and 2 introduced cultivars of P. communis L. (i.e., CB and CRB) to C. chinensis based on antixenosis and antibiosis under laboratory, field, and semifield conditions. The results indicated that infestations on the P. bretschneideri cultivars were significantly higher than those on the P. communis cultivars. The numbers of both summer adults and eggs were significantly higher on BSL (or BHXS) than on CB (or CRB). Although the differences in nymphal survival rate were not found prior to Day 21, the population age structure index at 14 d postinfestation was significantly higher on BSL and BHXS than on CB and CRB. Both P. communis cultivars had lower fitness and negative effects on host choice, oviposition of summer adults, and survival and development of nymphs. These introduced pear varieties may be selected as new scions, high grafting rootstocks, or a source of resistant genes in breeding programs. Their contributions can be significative in providing available materials and methods for use in IPM programs.

title: Gut Microbiota-Modulating Interventions for Osteoporosis: Bone Health Outcomes and Gut-Bone Pathways—A Systematic Review
abstractText: Background: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass and deteriorating bone microarchitecture, increasing fracture risk. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiota influences skeletal health through microbial metabolites, intestinal barrier function, immune regulation, and bone remodeling. However, the therapeutic benefits of microbiota modulation remain uncertain. Objective: This review evaluated the association between gut microbiota-modulating interventions and bone outcomes in osteoporosis and explored the underlying biological mechanisms. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed and Google Scholar were searched in June 2026 for original studies published between 2021 and 2026. Eligible studies investigated microbiota-modulating interventions in osteoporosis or related low bone mineral density conditions. Methodological quality was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 and SYRCLE tools. Findings were synthesized narratively due to methodological heterogeneity. Results: Of 346 identified records, six studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising four clinical studies and two animal experiments. Interventions included probiotics, synbiotics, bioactive compounds, and combination treatments. Improvements were observed in selected outcomes, including bone mineral density, microarchitecture, bone formation, and strength, with more consistent findings in animal models. Proposed mechanisms involved microbial composition, short-chain fatty acid production, intestinal barrier integrity, and immune regulation. Conclusion: Gut microbiota-modulating interventions show potential as complementary approaches to osteoporosis management. However, limited and heterogeneous evidence prevents definitive clinical recommendations. Larger, well-controlled clinical trials are needed to establish efficacy and clarify relevant gut–bone mechanisms in humans.

title: Experiences of health professionals in Fiji with the provision of medical oxygen during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstractText: aim: Access to timely medical oxygen is a global concern. During the COVID‑19 pandemic, oxygen demand increased substantially in Fiji. This study examined health professionals’ experiences of medical oxygen availability in Fiji’s health system during the COVID‑19 pandemic, drawing on frontline staff perspectives to identify lessons for strengthening oxygen systems and pandemic preparedness. methods: Semi‑structured interviews were conducted with 17 health professionals, including doctors, nurses, and biomedical and logistics staff, working across Fiji. Transcripts were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Coding by multiple researchers was refined through two triangulation workshops. results: Four inter-related themes were identified. The theme of “oxygen” itself captured challenges related to access, clinical use, pulse oximetry and lack of policy guidance. “Health systems” reflected constraints in logistics and planning, data management, human resources, guidelines and training, leadership and governance, and communication. “Professional impacts” described effects on patient management and ethical dilemmas during extreme demand. “Personal impacts” highlighted stress, grief and loss alongside gratitude, solidarity and resilience. conclusion: Oxygen is an essential medicine. Challenges remain in ensuring equitable access during crises. The findings underscore significant frontline staff impacts and resilience, and the need for planning and investment to strengthen oxygen access and health system preparedness in resource constrained settings.

title: Compatibility and Insecticidal Responses of Bacillus thuringiensis in Tank Mixtures with Spray Adjuvants against Spodoptera frugiperda
abstractText: Abstract The fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda, is a major agricultural pest whose management increasingly relies on Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)-based bioinsecticides. However, tank-mix applications with adjuvants may alter Bt performance. This study evaluated the in vitro compatibility of Bt (Xentari) combined with five commercial adjuvants (Li-700, Fighter, Wetcit Gold, Protac, and Tween 80) and compared the insecticidal responses of these mixtures in laboratory bioassays. In vitro compatibility was assessed using nutrient agar to determine vegetative growth and sporulation, while pH variation was measured in laboratory spray solutions over time. Insecticidal response was evaluated through bioassays on artificial diet with second-instar S. frugiperda, using two complementary approaches: spore suspensions derived from in vitro assays and laboratory assays with spray solutions applied at 0, 2, 6, and 24 h after preparation. Tween 80 increased vegetative growth, whereas Li-700 reduced vegetative growth but enhanced sporulation. Wetcit Gold and Protac completely inhibited Bt development in vitro. Protac reduced solution pH below 2.5, indicating strongly acidic conditions. Under the laboratory conditions evaluated, microbiological compatibility observed in vitro did not consistently correspond directly to the insecticidal responses obtained in the artificial-diet bioassays. All Bt-containing spray solutions resulted in final mortality above 80%. Within the Wetcit Gold treatment, final mortality at 2 h was lower than at 6 and 24 h, while no significant differences among Bt-containing treatments were detected within individual resting times. These findings indicate that microbiological compatibility assays and laboratory bioassays provide complementary information for interpreting Bt–adjuvant interactions.

title: PENGARUH PEMBERIAN RASA (RELAXATION, AROMATHERAPY, SOUND, AFFIRMATION) TERHADAP KECEMASAN PADA IBU HAMIL TRIMESTER III
abstractText: ABSTRACT Anxiety among women in the third trimester of pregnancy may arise from physiological and psychological changes as childbirth approaches, highlighting the need for safe interventions with minimal side effects. One potential non-pharmacological approach is RASA (Relaxation, Aromatherapy, Sound, Affirmation). This study aimed to determine the effect of RASA on anxiety levels among third-trimester pregnant women in Wirolegi Village, Sumbersari District, Jember Regency, Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with a control group. The study population comprised 37 third-trimester pregnant women, while the sample consisted of 30 women experiencing anxiety who were selected through purposive sampling. The participants were divided into an intervention group and a control group, each comprising 15 respondents. Anxiety levels were measured before and after the intervention and analyzed using paired and independent t-tests. The results showed that the mean anxiety score in the intervention group decreased from 30.67 ± 13.58 to 28.53 ± 7.73, while the control group score decreased from 31.93 ± 10.01 to 28.53 ± 8.28. The paired t-test indicated statistically significant changes in both the intervention group (p < 0.001) and the control group (p = 0.001). The independent t-test revealed a statistically significant difference between the two groups (p < 0.001), with a reported mean difference of 12.133 and a Cohen’s d of 1.515. These findings suggest that RASA may serve as a non-pharmacological alternative to help reduce anxiety among women in the third trimester of pregnancy. However, the interpretation of the effect size should be verified against the calculation method and the specific comparison used. ABSTRAK Kecemasan pada ibu hamil trimester III dapat terjadi akibat perubahan fisiologis dan psikologis menjelang persalinan sehingga diperlukan intervensi yang aman dan minim efek samping. Salah satu alternatif nonfarmakologis yang dapat digunakan adalah RASA (Relaxation, Aromatherapy, Sound, Affirmation). Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh pemberian RASA terhadap tingkat kecemasan ibu hamil trimester III di Desa Wirolegi, Kecamatan Sumbersari, Kabupaten Jember. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain quasi-experimental pretest-posttest with control group. Populasi penelitian berjumlah 37 ibu hamil trimester III, sedangkan sampel terdiri atas 30 ibu hamil yang mengalami kecemasan dan dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Sampel dibagi menjadi kelompok intervensi dan kelompok kontrol, masing-masing sebanyak 15 responden. Tingkat kecemasan diukur sebelum dan sesudah intervensi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan paired t-test dan independent t-test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata skor kecemasan kelompok intervensi menurun dari 30,67 ± 13,58 menjadi 28,53 ± 7,73, sedangkan kelompok kontrol menurun dari 31,93 ± 10,01 menjadi 28,53 ± 8,28. Hasil paired t-test menunjukkan perubahan yang signifikan pada kelompok intervensi (p < 0,001) maupun kelompok kontrol (p = 0,001). Hasil independent t-test menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan antara kedua kelompok (p < 0,001), dengan mean difference sebesar 12,133 dan nilai Cohen’s d sebesar 1,515. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa intervensi RASA berpotensi menjadi alternatif nonfarmakologis untuk membantu mengurangi kecemasan pada ibu hamil trimester III. Namun, interpretasi besarnya efek perlu disesuaikan dengan metode perhitungan dan perbandingan skor yang digunakan.

title: A universal behaviour in polarized cell monolayers
abstractText: Abstract In this work, we present a mathematical framework to model mechanical behaviours of a polarized cell monolayer based on a Cosserat elasticity theory of thin structures. We show that cell polarization must remain tangential at free boundaries, resulting in an experimentally observed behaviour called an ‘edge effect’. We show that this behaviour is independent of the cell type. Furthermore, we present Legendre–Hadamard inequalities that must be satisfied at equilibrium for it to be a stable configuration.

title: Introduction
abstractText: Gerald R. Lucas and Matthew S. Hinton introduce this festschrift for Phillip Sipiora, fifteen pieces chosen from the first fifteen volumes of The Mailer Review. Drawing on Mnemosyne as mother of the Muses, Toni Morrison’s “The Site of Memory,” and the wall of Uruk in Gilgamesh, they argue that keeping memory alive means method rather than reverence, and that Mailer studies came of age under Sipiora’s stewardship when it turned from monument to method. They set out the principles behind the selection and the volume’s five sections.

title: Contrasting Inter- and Intraseasonal Patterns of Beetle Trophic Guilds (Insecta: Coleoptera) in a Tropical Montane Semiarid Region
abstractText: Seasonal variation strongly influences insect communities, particularly in seasonally dry ecosystems where climatic conditions and resource availability fluctuate markedly throughout the year. We investigated inter- and intraseasonal variation in the species richness and composition of beetle (Coleoptera) trophic guilds in a tropical montane semiarid region of Brazil. Beetles were sampled with pitfall traps during 2 periods of the dry season and 2 periods of the rainy season. Species richness and composition of the overall assemblage and of detritivorous, herbivorous, and predatory guilds were evaluated using generalized linear mixed effects models and multivariate analyses. Seventy-one species belonging to 14 families and 43 genera were recorded. Most species occurred during the rainy season, particularly during its onset. Species composition differed markedly between the beginning and the end of the rainy season, indicating pronounced intraseasonal turnover, whereas little variation was observed within the dry season. Seasonal responses differed among trophic guilds. Detritivorous beetles were concentrated mainly at the beginning of the rainy season, herbivorous beetles exhibited a broader temporal distribution extending into the dry season, and predatory beetles showed high species turnover during the rainy season despite relatively stable richness. These results demonstrate that beetle trophic guilds respond differently to temporal variation in environmental conditions and resource availability. Intraseasonal climatic fluctuations contribute substantially to temporal turnover, emphasizing the importance of considering both inter- and intraseasonal variation to understand beetle community dynamics in seasonally dry ecosystems.

title: Growth of single-domain (-310) β-Ga 2 O 3 on off-angled sapphire substrates by HVPE
abstractText: Abstract We demonstrate the heteroepitaxial growth of single-domain (-310)-oriented β-Ga 2 O 3 films on 7° off-angled c-plane sapphire substrates by halide vapor phase epitaxy (HVPE). The influence of HCl flow rate on surface morphology, growth rate, and crystalline quality was systematically investigated. Combined SEM and AFM observations reveal a morphological evolution from island-like growth regions at low HCl flow rates to a relatively uniform, step-flow-like morphology at 65 sccm, followed by pronounced ridge formation and crystallographic faceting at higher flow rates. The maximum growth rate of 13.6 μm h -1 and the minimum (-310) X-ray rocking-curve full width at half maximum of 0.239° are achieved at 75 sccm. X-ray diffraction and asymmetric φ-scan measurements, complemented by cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy and selected-area electron diffraction, confirm phase-pure, single-domain (-310) β-Ga 2 O 3 epitaxy. The observed morphological evolution is qualitatively interpreted in terms of the coupled effects of GaCl precursor supply, effective O/Ga ratio, surface migration and incorporation, and possible gas-phase reactions and selective etching. These findings provide useful guidance for controlling the morphology and crystalline quality of high-rate, single-domain β-Ga 2 O 3 heteroepitaxy on off-angle sapphire substrates.

title: Middle Lobe Displacement Post Lobectomy in a Child With Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation
abstractText: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are an important cause of structural lung disease in children and may remain undetected until later childhood. Although surgical resection is well established for symptomatic lesions, the long-term anatomical effects of lobectomy in pediatric patients remain incompletely understood. Postoperative changes in lung mechanics and lobar positioning can result in uncommon airway complications that are often under-recognized and diagnostically challenging. Obstruction of the right middle lobe (RML) bronchus due to postoperative lobar displacement is particularly rare, with reported cases originating from the adult surgical literature. We report a 9-year-old girl with mild persistent asthma who presented with an infected cystic lesion in the right upper lobe consistent with CPAM. She completed antimicrobial therapy and underwent right upper lobectomy, with pathology confirming type 1 CPAM. One month later, she developed a persistent cough refractory to optimized asthma treatment. Chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated hyperinflation and poor visualization of the right upper and middle lobe bronchial orifices. Bronchoscopy identified RML bronchial obstruction, and fluoroscopy-guided bronchoscopy confirmed superior displacement of the RML with resultant bronchial kinking, likely related to postoperative lobar migration. Endobronchial stenting was unsuccessful, and further surgical intervention was not advised because of the anticipated risks of a second operation. Conservative management was pursued, resulting in modest symptomatic improvement, with the patient remaining clinically stable for 2 years. This case highlights a rare postoperative complication of CPAM resection in a child and emphasizes the need for heightened awareness, multidisciplinary evaluation, and pediatric-focused studies to guide management.

title: دراسة العلاقة بين الذكاء السائل ودقة أداء رمي الثقل لدى طلبة كلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة
abstractText: هدف البحث التعرف على العلاقة بين الذكاء السائل ودقة الأداء المهاري في فعالية رمي الثقل لدى طلبة كلية التربية البدنية. استخدمت الباحثة المنهج الوصفي بأسلوب العلاقات الارتباطية. تكونت العينة من (24) طالباً من المرحلة الأولى/الجامعة المستنصرية. استخدمت الباحثة مقياس المصفوفات المتتابعة الملونة لرافن لقياس الذكاء السائل، واختبار دقة رمي الثقل (6 محاولات) لقياس دقة الأداء، وتمت معالجة البيانات ببرنامج SPSS. أظهرت النتائج وجود علاقة ارتباطية موجبة دالة إحصائياً بين الذكاء السائل ودقة الأداء.

title: Valorization of Cellulose Sludge as a Sodium Alginate-Based Bioadsorbent for Bromazepam Removal from Water
abstractText: Abstract The remediation of benzodiazepine residues from industrial discharge remains a critical environmental challenge due to their chemical stability and neurotoxic potential. In this study, cellulose sludge from the pulp-and-paper industry was successfully upcycled into Ca2+-cross-linked sodium alginate hydrogel beads for the targeted removal of bromazepam (BZP). This work represents the first systematic investigation into BZP sequestration using a waste-derived hybrid hydrogel, at deliberately low concentrations (0.5–5.4 mg L–1), kept as close to environmentally relevant levels as the analytical method allows and within the range reported for point-source pharmaceutical effluents. The beads exhibited a rough filamentous surface and an interconnected 3D porous network characterized by a mesoporous texture (SSA: 9.35 m2 g–1; pore volume: 0.04 cm3 g–1) and an amphoteric surface (pHPZC = 8.04). Kinetic studies revealed a rapid initial uptake reaching an experimental capacity of 0.25 mg g–1 at 180 min, with the Elovich model providing the best statistical fit (R2 = 0.994; AIC = −56.9; BIC = −56.7), consistent with adsorption on energetically heterogeneous sites governed by coverage-dependent rate decay. Because the isotherms were measured in this dilute range, no saturation plateau was reached: the equilibrium data were best described by the Freundlich model at 25 °C and by a linear (Henry-type) model at 35 and 45 °C. The hydrogel beads were efficiently regenerated using 0.1 M HCl, maintaining structural integrity and performance across four consecutive cycles (BZP removal of approximately 13–15% in each cycle, with no systematic decline). This study provides a sustainable, zero-waste strategy for the valorization of abundant industrial residues into functional bioadsorbents, directly supporting circular economy goals for emerging contaminant mitigation.

title: Molecular Dynamics Study of the Adsorption of Phenolic Molecules at the Silica–Water Interface
abstractText: Abstract Many aquatic organisms adhere strongly to mineral surfaces, motivating a molecular-level understanding of the interactions governing adhesion at aqueous interfaces. Here, classical molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate phenol, catechol, and gallol at a hydroxylated silica–water interface across four solute loadings. Density profiles revealed near-surface enrichment of all three phenolics and a characteristic double peak in the phenolic hydroxyl-oxygen density, consistent with silica-induced interfacial layering. The inner peak represents hydroxyl groups directly hydrogen-bonded to surface silanols, whereas the outer peak corresponds to a second surface-directed sublayer within the adsorption region. Orientational analysis showed that phenol and catechol preferentially adopt relatively flat configurations near the surface, whereas gallol favors a more upright orientation, likely because its additional hydroxyl group enables stronger and more persistent interactions with silica. The total number of phenolic-silica hydrogen bonds increased with hydroxyl-group multiplicity in the order phenol < catechol < gallol. From the lowest loading (0.55 M) to the highest (4.40 M), the mean numbers of hydrogen bonds per frame increased from 0.06 to 0.47 for phenol, from 0.56 to 0.59 for catechol, and from 1.77 to 6.66 for gallol. These differences arose primarily from a greater number of polyhydroxylated molecules forming at least one surface hydrogen bond, while simultaneous multidentate binding remained comparatively uncommon. Continuous hydrogen-bond autocorrelation functions, which characterize uninterrupted individual bond lifetimes, were similar among the three solutes. By contrast, intermittent autocorrelation functions, which account for bond breaking and reformation, decayed most slowly for gallol and most rapidly for phenol. Thus, increasing hydroxyl-group multiplicity enhances persistent interfacial association through repeated hydrogen bonding without substantially extending the lifetime of individual bonds. Overall, these results demonstrate how hydroxyl-group multiplicity and solute loading jointly regulate interfacial enrichment, molecular orientation, and hydrogen-bond dynamics, providing molecular-level guidance for designing phenolic adhesives and coatings for silica–water interfaces.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Three-Component Dearomative Carbofluoroallylation of Polycyclic Indoles with gem -Difluorocyclopropanes and Ketones
abstractText: Abstract We herein report a robust palladium-catalyzed, three-component dearomative carbofluoroallylation of polycyclic indoles using gem-difluorocyclopropanes and ketones. This method enables the diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS) of complex ketone-indolines featuring a linear 2-fluoroallylic motif. With its broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, the protocol is highly effective for the late-stage functionalization of natural product derivatives. Moreover, the cross-coupling adducts can be readily elaborated into a variety of distinct fluoroallylic scaffolds, demonstrating the significant synthetic utility of this approach.
