title: Counterintuitive Photoresponsiveness of Thermoresponsive Polyacrylamides: Effects of Azobenzene Content and Amino Acid Spacers
abstractText: Abstract Four sets of dual-responsive statistical copolymers are synthesized from N,N-dimethylacrylamide and acrylamide comonomers bearing photoresponsive 4-aminoazobenzene (AzBn) side groups linked by various amino acid spacers. In aqueous solution, the copolymers exhibit lower critical solution temperature (LCST) behavior modulated by the E-to-Z photoisomerization of AzBn. Their cloud point temperatures (TCP) decrease markedly with increasing AzBn content and, at contents of 8 mol % and above, are counterintuitively lower in the—a priori—more polar-Z-state, with photoinduced shifts reaching –16 °C. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) on three exemplary copolymers support the formation of compact, spherical single-chain nanoparticles (SCNPs), ascribed to hydrophobic association of AzBn. In most cases, photoisomerization induces only modest changes in global SCNP dimensions, but substantially alters the LCST behavior. These results indicate that the AzBn content primarily determines the overall photoresponsive trend, whereas spacer-dependent differences in local chemical and steric environment further modulate the thermoresponsive behavior.

title: Moringa oleifera Alginate-Based Beads for Adsorption of Selected Heavy Metals: Preparation, Kinetics, Isotherms, and Reusability Studies
abstractText: Abstract Moringa oleifera (MO) leaf powder, a low-cost natural resource, has been extensively used for the removal of heavy metals from water. To overcome challenges associated with powdered adsorbents, including difficult separation and low recovery, this study details the synthesis and evaluation of MO-alginate (MO-Alg) bead adsorbents for the adsorption of arsenic, cadmium, iron, chromium, zinc, and lead from oil-polluted aqueous samples. The beads were prepared through ionic gelation using sodium alginate (SA) as an encapsulation matrix with varying MO loadings. SEM analysis revealed that MO-Alg beads were spherical with a rough and cracked surface texture compared to smooth pristine sodium alginate (SA) beads, while XRD analysis confirmed the amorphous nature of both materials. At pH 5, MO (4 g) beads achieved the highest adsorption efficiencies. Kinetic studies followed the pseudo-second-order model, while equilibrium data fitted the Langmuir model for As(III) and Cr(VI) and the Freundlich isotherm model for Cd(II), Pb(II), Zn(II), and Fe(III). The Langmuir isotherm model estimated maximum adsorption capacities of 44.22, 61.11, 41.16, 59.14, 55.22, and 76.69 mg/g for As(III), Cd(II), Cr(VI), Fe(III), Pb(II), and Zn(II), respectively, at 25 °C. Negative ΔG° and positive ΔH° values over 25–45 °C confirmed that the adsorption process was spontaneous and endothermic. Reusability tests demonstrated that MO-Alg (1:1) beads maintained strong adsorption performance after seven regeneration cycles with removal efficiencies above 70% for Pb(II), Cd(II), and Zn(II), while As(III), Cr(VI), and Fe(III) remained effective up to six cycles with efficiencies above 60%. Overall, MO-Alg beads have great potential as an inexpensive sorbent for the removal of toxic heavy metals.

title: ANALISIS PENENTUAN KELAYAKAN IZIN PENEBANGAN POHON BERDASARKAN DATA PERIZINAN MENGGUNAKAN METODE DECISION TREE (STUDI KASUS: DINAS LINGKUNGAN HIDUP KOTA BINJAI)
abstractText: Pada Dinas Lingkungan Hidup Kota Binjai sebagai sumber informasi untuk mengetahui pola penentuan kelayakan izin. Proses penentuan yang melibatkan beberapa atribut membutuhkan analisis yang sistematis agar pola keputusan dari data sebelumnya dapat diketahui. Penelitian ini bertujuan menerapkan algoritma Decision Tree C4.5 untuk mengklasifikasikan kelayakan izin penebangan pohon berdasarkan data perizinan yang tersedia. Data yang digunakan sebanyak 127 data dengan atribut Jenis Pohon, Umur Pohon, Diameter, Kondisi Pohon, Lokasi, Alasan, dan Keputusan sebagai label. Proses pengolahan data dilakukan menggunakan RapidMiner, dengan pembagian 100 data sebagai training dan 27 data sebagai testing. Pembentukan model menggunakan kriteria Gain Ratio, sedangkan evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan Accuracy, Recall, Precision, dan Confusion Matrix. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Kondisi Pohon menjadi root node pada struktur Decision Tree, kemudian proses klasifikasi pada kondisi tertentu dilanjutkan berdasarkan Umur Pohon, Diameter, Lokasi, dan Alasan. Hasil pengujian terhadap 27 data menunjukkan seluruh data berhasil diklasifikasikan dengan benar, dengan nilai Accuracy, Weighted Mean Recall, dan Weighted Mean Precision masing-masing sebesar 100%. Dengan demikian, algoritma Decision Tree C4.5 dapat menghasilkan pola klasifikasi dan aturan keputusan sebagai bahan pendukung penentuan kelayakan izin penebangan pohon.

title: RANCANG BANGUN PLATFORM AUDIT DAN MONITORING KEAMANAN SERVER TERPUSAT BERBASIS WEB DENGAN ARSITEKTUR CONTROLLER-AGENT
abstractText: Linux server infrastructure in educational institutions is vulnerable to cybersecurity threats including misconfiguration, privileged access abuse, and unauthorized modification of critical configuration files. This research designs and develops SecureOps, a centralized web-based server security audit and monitoring platform with a Controller-Agent architecture. Developed using FastAPI, React 18, Linux PAM + JWT, and Tailscale WireGuard, SecureOps integrates six security modules: permission audit, SHA-256 FIM, sudo monitor, activity logs, system health, and SSH terminal. Black-box testing of 62 test cases yielded a 100% pass rate with average API response time of 187ms under 50 concurrent users. Usability evaluation using SUS produced an average score of 82.3 ("Good"). These results demonstrate that SecureOps effectively meets multi-server security monitoring needs.

title: EMSA-YOLO: An Enhanced Multiscale Attention Model for Pavement Defect Detection
abstractText: Abstract Accurate and efficient identification of pavement defects is crucial for reducing traffic accident rates and ensuring the safety of road users’ lives and property. To effectively address the multiscale issue in pavement defect detection and significantly improve the detection accuracy of pavement defects, this study takes the YOLOv8 model as the basic framework. A new detection model is designed through targeted improvements, which is named Enhanced Multiscale Attention-YOLO (EMSA-YOLO), which integrates multiscale attention mechanisms with large-target feature extraction capabilities. Firstly, to enhance the extraction of defect features across multiple spatial scales, the EMSA module is designed to expand the receptive field and incorporate multiscale contextual information through the application of a learned weight matrix. Secondly, DySample is employed to optimize the upsampling process in the neck network, yielding clearer fused feature images and enhancing the detection accuracy of small-sized potholes. Finally, we add a new P6 large target detection layer to expand the receptive field and capture multiscale features, which enables the model to capture deeper semantic features and improve the detection of longitudinal and transverse cracks. Experimental results on the RDD2022 dataset demonstrate that the EMSA-YOLO achieves 84.1% mAP@50 and 57.5% mAP@50-95, outperforming the baseline by 2.1% and 1.7%, respectively. Significant accuracy improvements are observed in three critical defect categories: transverse crack with a 2.4% increase, alligator crack with a 4.8% increase, and potholes with a 1.4% increase compared to the baseline performance.

title: Tripartite Quantum Coherence and Nonlocality Swapping via POVM Measurements
abstractText: Abstract We investigate tripartite quantum coherence and nonlocality swapping via generalized positive operator-valued measure (POVM) measurements in the GHZ and W -state bases, performed locally at a single node of a three-party quantum network. The resulting post-measurement states are characterized using the tripartite Bell-Mermin-Klyshko inequalities and two standard coherence measures: the l 1 -norm coherence and the relative entropy coherence. We find that both coherence and nonlocality can be successfully transferred to the remote subsystem through generalized measurements, with the degree of swapping depending on the POVM strength, the initial entanglement, and the choice of measurement basis. For product-state inputs, no swapping occurs. These results establish a framework for multipartite correlation swapping via POVMs and may find applications in quantum repeater architectures and quantum networks.

title: Use of mobile devices and their relationship with academic performance and student behavior in Business Management Engineering students at the Instituto Tecnológico de Nuevo León
abstractText: This study analyzed the relationship between mobile device use, academic performance, and student behavior among Business Management Engineering students at the Technological Institute of Nuevo León. A mixed-methods, descriptive-correlational design was employed through a self-administered questionnaire applied to 300 students and a focus group with 25 participants. Results revealed that 61.7% of students frequently used mobile devices for academic purposes; however, social media and entertainment remained common non-academic activities. Additionally, 69.4% reported being easily distracted while studying, and 64.3% acknowledged procrastination behaviors associated with device use. Spearman correlation analysis identified a significant negative relationship between distraction and academic performance [rs = -0.124, p = .032], and a positive relationship between sleep duration and academic performance [rs = 0.137, p = .030]. Findings suggest that the educational impact of mobile devices depends largely on students self-regulation and patterns of use.

title: People and bats in Fiji: perceptions and interactions
abstractText: Abstract The management of wild bat populations often presents challenges in balancing the needs of biodiversity conservation and public health risks from zoonotic diseases. In Fiji, the most important recognized zoonotic infection is Leptospira, which was recently detected in wild bat populations. Five out of six species of Fijian bats are considered threatened to critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. This study investigates the perceptions of bats by people in Fiji and aims to identify and quantify the reported frequency and types of interactions between bats and people. In this mixed-methods study, 198 Fijian people were interviewed across the three main islands of Fiji: Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni. Bats were generally perceived positively (63%, 125/198), mostly because they are perceived to be ‘clean, healthy and tasty’ meat sources (73%, 134/184). The majority of participants consume and come into contact with bats or with their urine, faeces, blood and saliva. Older adults, men and those who recognize that bats can cause harm are more likely to contact bats in Fiji. Quantifying these interactions and identifying other risk factors for bat exposure is an important step in targeting conservation efforts, community engagement and education, as well as determining at-risk groups for possible zoonotic pathogen exposure.

title: An integrated gut phage catalogue of nonhuman primates reveals functional adaptation to host ecology and evolutionary link to humans
abstractText: Abstract Nonhuman primates (NHPs), the closest evolutionary relatives of humans, are pivotal models for biomedical and ecological research. Gut phage are recognized as critical modulators of gut microbial communities; however, comprehensive insight into gut phage of NHPs is lacking. We used gut metagenomes spanning 25 NHP species and constructed an integrated gut phage catalogue (IGPC) comprising 11 389 nonredundant phage genomes. Our results revealed that the composition and function of NHP gut phage were significantly influenced by host clade, dietary niche and lifestyle. Host clade exerted a stronger influence than dietary niche on gut phage diversity. The lifestyle of NHPs influenced gut phage diversity and altered auxiliary metabolic gene profiles for different NHP species. Comparatively, 78.5% of IGPC phages were detected in human guts, with higher prevalence in nonindustrialized human guts. crAss-like phage—the most prevalent human-associated phage—were abundant in NHP guts, while exhibiting distinct evolutionary differences from crAss-like phage of humans. These findings comprehensively characterize the gut phageome of NHPs, revealing NHP host-driven and environment-driven functional adaptations, and provide an evolutionary understanding of the gut phageome between NHPs and humans.

title: Formal divergence and legal relation preservation in Hong Kong judgment translation
abstractText: Abstract Legal English secures precision through dense qualificational syntax, and the evaluation of machine-translated legal texts often reads lower structural complexity as weaker legal precision. Whether formal simplification actually entails the loss of legally relevant relations has rarely been tested. This study examines the question in 57 Chinese-language Hong Kong judgments, comparing their official English translations with DeepSeek-V3.2 and ChatGPT output generated under a minimal prompt. Relative to the official translations, both model translations are shorter, lexically denser and markedly lower in subordination and complex nominal density. Their higher all-word lexical diversity lies in function words and has no counterpart in content words. A prespecified relation-level analysis then traced 192 source instances of qualification and scope marking into all three versions. Each version preserved the traced relations in over 97 % of its evaluable renderings, 98.06 % when the three versions are pooled. Of the eleven shifts, two occur in the official translations, five in DeepSeek and four in ChatGPT. The judgments with the greatest complex nominal divergence showed no larger model excess of shifts. The shifts that altered the reading of a judgment included changes in quantifier force, party coverage, attribution and restrictive scope, and the aggregate profile did not identify where they occurred. The findings separate formal simplification from relational loss. Legal precision in translated judgments is better evaluated through relational fidelity than through structural density, while corpus profiles remain appropriate for describing how production conditions package legal meaning.

title: Probing Rigidity and Fluidity of the Hydrophobic Region of Liposomes Using FTIR and 2D IR Spectroscopies
abstractText: Abstract Rigidity and fluidity of a lipid bilayer’s hydrophobic interior in unilamellar liposomes were evaluated using alkyl-azide-type probes for linear infrared (FTIR) and two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopies. When embedded into a bilayer of DPPC liposomes, the probes, azido-(CH2)n-COOH with n = 6, 8, 10, 13, 15 (denoted as aznAC), position their azido moieties at specific depths in the bilayer, defined by the alkyl tether length (n). The N3 moiety’s asymmetric stretching mode, νas, at ca. 2100 cm–1 shows abrupt changes in its peak width when the DPPC bilayer undergoes an Lβ–Lα phase transition, thus demonstrating probe sensitivity to the rigidity of the bilayer. Temperature dependences for the νas peak width show a sharp change at the phase transition temperature, Tph, for every depth (n), except for n = 6, although the magnitude of the sharp change at Tph differs for different depths, indicating that the packing order depends greatly on the depth in the bilayer. The range of the νas peak width change for az10AC is remarkable, with widths of 9.5 cm–1 at 25 °C and 22.7 cm–1 at 45 °C, which is a 2.4-fold change. A detailed DFT computational analysis was performed to understand the origin of the high sensitivity of the probes to the rigidity of the environment. It was established that the softness of the CNN angle (θ) and the presence of the θ-dependent multiple strong Fermi resonances with interaction energy exceeding 20 cm–1 result in severe broadening of νas. Furthermore, we showed that specific restrictions in the θ-angle distribution, occurring, for example, in bilayers in the gel phase reduce the νas peak width greatly. Spectral diffusion 2D IR measurements revealed the time scales of the conformational relaxation of the bilayer for az10AC in liposomes, which were found to be ca. 6 ps with a significant static component in the gel phase (25 °C) and ca. 2 ps in the liquid-crystal phase (45 °C). Such a large difference in decay times between the two limiting phases makes the aznAC probes sensitive reporters of bilayer fluidity. An isotopically edited compound, 15(N3)-(CH2)10-COOH (15az10AC), was also tested as a probe for the rigidity of the environment. While the width of the νas,15 peak at 2028 cm–1 is narrower than that of 14az10AC in the same environment, it still shows high sensitivity to the rigidity of the environment. DFT-based modeling revealed that a smaller number of Fermi resonances in 15aznAC is the reason for its narrower peak width. Simultaneous use of the two probes, 14aznAC and 15aznAC, was shown to be practical for simultaneously probing two different membrane regions.

title: Gallstone ileus of the large bowel presenting as a post-operative complication following elective knee arthroplasty
Evolutionary shifts in condition-transfer effects but not anticipatory maternal effects in Trinidadian killifish ( Anablepsoides hartii )
abstractText: Abstract Transgenerational plasticity (TGP) shapes offspring phenotypes independent of changes in DNA sequence. However, it remains unclear whether transgenerational plasticity primarily reflects adaptive anticipatory adjustments to predicted future environments or condition-dependent carryover from the parental energetic state. Because traits differ in their functional roles within life-history architecture, selection may favour distinct cross-generational mechanisms depending on the ecological context. We tested these alternatives using Trinidadian killifish (Anablepsoides hartii), which are locally adapted to either high-predation (HP) or predator-free killifish-only (KO) environments. Predation regime structures population density and per capita resource availability, making food availability an ecologically realistic proxy for the pathways through which predation regimes influence maternal conditions and transgenerational responses. Therefore, we experimentally manipulated the maternal (F2) and offspring (F3) food environments using a split-brood design and quantified the offspring body mass, body condition and egg development rate. Offspring body mass was overwhelmingly determined by the immediate food environment. By contrast, the egg development rate was strongly influenced by the maternal food environment. This condition-transfer effect was much stronger in the high-predation population. We found little evidence of anticipatory effects for any trait. Our results indicate that the evolution of condition-dependent maternal effects may represent a primary adaptive pathway when selection acts strongly on life-history pacing, helping reconcile mixed empirical support for anticipatory transgenerational plasticity.

title: Cognitive offloading dalam pembelajaran di era generative AI: Literasi AI untuk mendorong cognitive empowerment mahasiswa
abstractText: Kajian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis bagaimana cognitive offloading melalui penggunaan generative AI (GenAI) dapat memengaruhi cognitive empowerment dan mengidentifikasi peran literasi AI dalam proses tersebut. Permasalahan kajian ini berfokus pada bagaimana pengalihan beban kognitif kepada AI memengaruhi kapasitas belajar mahasiswa dan bagaimana kemampuan literasi AI oleh mahasiswa dapat mencegah berkembangnya ketergantungan kognitif. Metode yang digunakan adalah kajian konseptual melalui telaah literatur integratif terhadap literatur mengenai cognitive offloading, literasi AI, GenAI, metakognisi, dan pembelajaran mandiri. Literasi AI berperan sebagai kompetensi pengarah melalui kemampuan memahami keterbatasan AI, menggunakan AI secara strategis, mengevaluasi keluaran, mengatur tingkat ketergantungan, dan melakukan refleksi terhadap proses belajar. Kajian ini menegaskan bahwa penggunaan GenAI dapat bergeser dari pengurangan beban berpikir menuju penguatan kapasitas belajar apabila mahasiswa tetap mempertahankan cognitive agency dalam proses pembelajaran.

Digital citizen science and perceived scientific literacy among high school students: a descriptive study on participation in biodiversity activities
abstractText: This study examined the self-perceived scientific literacy of 50 high school students after participating in digital citizen science projects focused on biodiversity documentation. To move beyond basic descriptive reporting and toward more comprehensive evaluation, a mixed-methods approach was employed, integrating quantitative survey data with qualitative content analysis of students' reflective logs and open-ended feedback. A 20-item Likert scale, organized into four dimensions [data handling, understanding of scientific processes, use of evidence, and environmental commitment], was administered. The findings point out a high level of self-reported scientific literacy [M = 4.08; SD = 0.54], with particularly strong scores in environmental engagement. Overall, the results suggest that incorporating technological tools into biology education provides a pedagogical framework for connecting scientific theory with practical ecological action among students.

title: STRUCTURAL DESIGN AND LAYOUT OF A COOKING VEHICLE MODIFIED FROM HEAVY-DUTY TRUCK CHASSIS
abstractText: To meet the needs of centralized meal preparation for multiple personnel in scenarios such as field emergencies, military garrison training, engineering construction, and large-scale events, this paper introduces the structural design of a cooking vehicle modified from a heavy-duty cargo vehicle chassis. Based on a SITRAK heavy-duty cargo vehicle second-type chassis with a maximum total mass of 16 t, the vehicle was modified through alterations to the body structure, interior decoration, water supply and drainage systems, and power supply system to meet the functional requirements of a mobile kitchen. The interior of the vehicle body is divided into three functional zones: water supply and purification area, cooking and processing area, and storage and preservation area. These areas are sequentially equipped with water pump and water purifier systems, water heaters, clean water tanks, rice steamers, meat mincers and vegetable cutters, workbenches, sinks, freezers, storage cabinets, double-burner stoves, spice boxes and cooking oil, and other equipment. External facilities include side pull-out ladders, rear pull-out ladders, wastewater tank, cable reel, support leg controls, gasoline generator, inverter and battery, support legs, city power input, rear single door, roof side lighting, and side roof access ladder. The vehicle adopts a multi-power supply system prioritizing city power with generator backup and inverter-battery supplementation, along with monitoring and alarm functions for water level, fuel level, and wastewater tank overflow. Through reasonable layout and structural design, the vehicle features flexibility, efficient meal preparation, and safety reliability, capable of meeting the daily dining needs of multiple personnel under field conditions.

title: “Who Touched Me?” Contagion and the Gesture of Touch in Two Lukan Healing Narratives
abstractText: Abstract In this article I look at two passages from the Gospel of Luke in which touch as a gesture plays a significant role: Jesus’ healing of a man with lepra through touch (Luke 5:12–16), and the woman with the flow of blood who touches Jesus (Luke 8:43–48). The article addresses the significance of touch in these texts and looks at the correlation between touch and notions of illness and wellbeing. I analyze the passages through the theoretical lens of gesture, as developed by Judith Butler, asking what the gesture of touch affects in and beyond the narrative. I argue that haptic gestures have effects on two levels. The first level is the effects on the bodies of the characters in the story, and the second level is the effects on the expansion of the gospel. It is suggested that the gesture of touch simultaneously moves and re-moves in these two narratives. While the illness is re-moved through the touching of Jesus, the gospel continues to spread through rumors of Jesus’ healing powers. The gospel thus seems to imitate the miasmatic character of contagious diseases.

title: Toxicity Activity of Five Plant Extracts against Tetranychus truncatus (Acari: Tetranychidae) and Its Predatory Mite Amblyseius longispinosus (Acari: Phytoseiidae)
abstractText: Tetranychus truncatus Ehara (Acari: Tetranychidae) is one of the major economically important mite pests of numerous plant species. The predatory mite Amblyseius longispinosus (Evans) (Acari: Phytoseiidae) has been successfully used in biological control programs. This study evaluated the contact toxicity activities of ethanol extracts from 5 plants—Cymbopogon nardus (L.) Rendle, Ocimum basilicum L., Ocimum sanctum L., Andrographis paniculata (Burm.f.) Nees, and Stemona tuberosa Lour.—against T. truncatus and A. longispinosus. The ethanol plant extracts revealed different toxicity activity against T. truncatus and A. longispinosus. At concentrations of 7–9% (w/v), Cy. nardus and S. tuberosa extracts showed significant direct contact toxicity against T. truncatus adults, resulting in mortality rates of 64.00–70.67 and 51.33–55.00%, respectively, at 3 d after treatment. Application of 3–9% concentrations of Cy. nardus, 5–9% concentrations of O. basilicum and O. sanctum, and 9% concentrations of A. paniculata to T. truncatus eggs reduced egg viability, with >50% unhatched eggs 4 d following treatment. Concentrations of 5–9% of Cy. nardus and O. sanctum extracts were moderately toxic to A. longispinosus in residual contact toxicity, with mortality ranging from 22.67–34.67 and 22.67–29.33%, respectively, at 3 d after exposure. Based on our findings, extracts of Cy. nardus and T. tuberosa show promise as botanical acaricides for controlling T. truncatus adults, whereas extracts of Cy. nardus, O. basilicum, O. sanctum, and A. paniculata may be effective for the control of T. truncatus eggs. Furthermore, Cy. nardus and O. sanctum extracts negatively affected A. longispinosus.

title: Drivers of zoonotic spillover at human–domestic animal–wildlife interfaces: a multi-species model incorporating wildlife chronic stress
abstractText: Abstract Zoonotic disease emergence at the wildlife–domestic animal–human interface results from a complex interplay of ecological, physiological and anthropogenic factors. Here, we have developed a multi-environment, multi-host compartmental model to identify key drivers of spillover risk across urban, rural and natural environments. The framework incorporates heterogeneous host populations, inter-species contacts and host movement, and includes wildlife chronic stress as one factor influencing susceptibility, transmissibility and recovery. Sensitivity analyses show that domestic animal populations at agricultural interfaces strongly amplify spillover risk through their recovery dynamics and per-contact transmission probabilities, while within-wildlife transmission across environments also shapes system dynamics. Chronic stress effects can further increase spillover risk, and the model indicates that reducing wildlife stress alongside improving domestic animal health and management can markedly lower the likelihood of cross-species transmission. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining ecological conditions that reduce chronic physiological stress in wildlife populations and integrating physiological and ecological data into epidemiological modelling. Such models can inform both bottom-up interventions targeting domestic animals and top-down strategies that sustain resilient wildlife communities and, thereby, mitigate zoonotic spillover.

Metode pelaksanaan meliputi tahap persiapan, sosialisasi, workshop interaktif, praktik menulis, pendampingan, dan evaluasi produk karya siswa. title: SARS-CoV-2 exposure in deer increases with use of human-modified habitat
abstractText: Abstract Deer can transmit severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) to humans and harbour human-extinct variants. Despite this public health threat, ecological mechanisms driving exposure patterns in deer populations remain poorly understood. Our objective was to identify behavioural risk factors by linking serostatus of individual deer to their movement and space use using multilevel logistic regression. We examined serosurveillance data of white-tailed (Odocoileus virginianus) and mule deer (O. hemionus) wearing global positioning system devices across an urban–rural gradient in the United States (1151 individuals, 20 sites, 8 states). Seropositivity was positively associated with average human footprint index and negatively associated with average SARS-CoV-2 human wastewater concentration. Seropositivity was not associated with time spent in GAP-modelled deer habitat. Together, these findings provide evidence that human-to-deer transmission could be a primary source of deer SARS-CoV-2 exposure and deer populations may struggle to maintain transmission without repeated spillover from humans. Integrating human and environmental indices with movement behaviours and space use can thus clarify pathways that facilitate cross-species transmission in wildlife.

title: Effects of Tiger Tail Sea Cucumber Bohadschia argus on Wound Healing In Vitro and In Vivo Using an Acute Rat Model Infected with Staphylococcus aureus
abstractText: Abstract Infectious wounds caused by Staphylococcus aureus remain a significant clinical challenge due to delayed healing and increasing antimicrobial resistance, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the wound-healing potential of the ethanol extract of the tiger tail sea cucumber Bohadschia argus (EEBA) through integrated in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Phytochemical profiling using LC-HRMS identified 260 metabolites, and 12 prioritized compounds were selected for molecular docking analysis. EEBA demonstrated concentration-dependent antioxidant activity in the nitric oxide scavenging assay and inhibitory effects on protein denaturation, indicating anti-inflammatory potential, although differences compared to controls were not statistically significant (p > 0.05). In an excisional wound model in Staphylococcus aureus-infected Wistar rats, topical application of 1% EEBA accelerated wound contraction and improved macroscopic healing compared to the negative control. Histopathological evaluation revealed reduced inflammatory cell infiltration, enhanced fibroblast proliferation, increased angiogenesis, and improved collagen organization across the inflammatory, proliferative, and maturation phases. Hemolysis testing confirmed good biocompatibility with negligible erythrocyte lysis (<5%). Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding affinities of selected compounds toward key inflammatory targets, including TNF-α, NF-κB, and FLAP, as well as antibacterial targets relevant to Staphylococcus aureus, namely, DNA gyrase-B, dihydrofolate reductase, and penicillin-binding protein. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic insights into the potential wound-healing and antibacterial activities of EEBA. Overall, EEBA exhibits promising wound-healing activity in an infected wound model through modulation of oxidative stress and inflammatory pathways, with selected metabolites also showing potential interactions with bacterial targets associated with S. aureus infection. These findings support the potential development of EEBA as a natural therapeutic candidate for infected wound management.

title: Efeitos Fitotóxicos Subletais e Espécie-Dependentes do Elutriato da Fração Fina Minerada de Aterros Sanitários Avaliados por Bioensaios com Sementes
abstractText: A Fração Fina do Minerado (FFM), oriunda da mineração de aterros sanitários, apresenta potencial para reaproveitamento ambiental, mas demanda avaliação ecotoxicológica quanto aos seus efeitos biológicos. Este estudo investigou a fitotoxicidade do elutriato da FFM (EFFM) por meio de bioensaios com sementes de Allium cepa, Solanum lycopersicum e Eruca sativa, utilizando germinação e alongamento radicular como parâmetros biológicos. A germinação não diferiu significativamente do controle (p > 0,05) para todas as espécies. Entretanto, o alongamento radicular apresentou diferenças significativas entre concentrações (p < 0,05), revelando efeitos subletais dependentes da espécie. A. cepa e E. sativa exibiram padrão compatível com resposta hormética, com estímulo em concentrações baixas a intermediárias e redução em níveis mais elevados. S. lycopersicum apresentou tendência predominantemente inibitória nas maiores concentrações, com toxicidade classificada como baixa a moderada. Os resultados demonstram que o EFFM exerce efeitos fitotóxicos subletais e espécie-dependentes, reforçando a importância de abordagens multiespécies e do alongamento radicular como indicador sensível na avaliação de materiais residuais destinados à aplicação ambiental.

Fluoride-Free Siloxane Circularity at Room Temperature: Tetrabutylammonium Hydroxide as a Dual-Functional De- and Repolymerization Initiator for Silicone Oils, Elastomers, and Hybrid Coatings
abstractText: Abstract With increasing EU restrictions on fluoride chemistries and their toxicity related to the potential generation of hydrofluoric acid (HF) as well as their corrosivity, there is an urgent need to develop fluoride-free depolymerization methods to enable safe and sustainable siloxane recycling. In this regard, we here present a fluoride-free, at room-temperature (RT) operating depolymerization method, where tetrabutylammonium hydroxide (TBAOH), identified as a highly effective dual-functional de- and repolymerization initiator, transforms silicone-based elastomers into reusable cyclic siloxanes. Thereby, the solvent/polymer ratio (v/w) is the key for controlling the product distribution: at 10/1 (v/w), the depolymerization mixture shifts from D4-rich to high proportions of byproducts greater than 40 mol % and ultimately stops the process, leaving solid educt silicone at even lower dilutions. Under optimized reaction conditions above a threshold of 0.29/1 (w/w) for the TBAOH/polymer ratio, a relative proportion of up to 88 mol % cyclic siloxanes (D3 to D5), with D4 as the main product, is obtained. This corresponds to 77 mol % absolute NMR conversion into cyclic siloxanes. Additionally, it is worth noting that the fluoride-free, RT operating reaction conditions are effective for a very broad educt scope ranging from linear polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) oils, (filled) Pt-cross-linked silicone elastomers, to inorganic–organic hybrid polymers and coatings. Compared to sodium hydroxide (NaOH) as an alkaline reference, TBAOH affords fewer noncyclic byproducts (12–26 mol % vs 25–30 mol %) and a higher D3 (4–14 mol % vs 1–3 mol %) relative proportion, highlighting its distinct reactivity. Fluoride-free siloxane circularity is demonstrated at RT by two complementary repolymerization routes. Within the first method, TBAOH uniquely acts as the initiator for both the depolymerization and the subsequent anionic ring-opening polymerization (AROP) without prior workup, while the second involves the isolation of cyclic siloxanes followed by base-catalyzed AROP. Thus, this TBAOH-enabled, fluoride-free depolymerization method, which operates at RT, provides tunable product distributions and a broad substrate applicability for practical silicone circularity.

title: A frugal automated contact angle analyser for low-cost surface wettability characterization
abstractText: Abstract Contact angle measurement is a fundamental technique for evaluating surface wettability in materials science, biomedical engineering and coating technologies. However, the high cost of commercial contact angle analysers limits access to surface characterization, particularly in resource-limited laboratories. This study presents a low-cost automated contact angle analyser developed using frugal engineering principles and open-source hardware. The system integrates Arduino-based control, NEMA 17 stepper-motor actuation, automated microdroplet dispensing, smartphone-based optical imaging and a 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA) framework. A calibrated 330-step dispensing cycle generated reproducible 5 μl water droplets, with fixed optical alignment minimized operator variability. Wettability measurements were performed on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and aluminium substrates and analysed using ImageJ. Mean contact angles were 108.5° for PTFE, 73.9° for PVC and 85.8° for aluminium, closely matching published literature values. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) demonstrated significant differences between substrates (p < 0.001), with measurement variability of ±2.3° indicated good repeatability. The total fabrication cost was £114.26, representing approximately 99% cost reduction compared with commercial instruments. The proposed platform demonstrates that automated, reproducible surface wettability characterization can be achieved using low-cost, open-source instrumentation, providing an accessible solution for research, education and engineering laboratories while broadening access to advanced materials characterization.

title: Clinical outcomes after diaphragm plication for diaphragm paralysis: a single New Zealand centre retrospective cohort study
abstractText: aim: The aim of this study was to assess clinical outcomes, including breathlessness, after diaphragm plication in patients with symptomatic diaphragm paralysis. methods: A retrospective cohort study of all patients undergoing diaphragm plication at Christchurch Hospital between 1 January 2018 and 31 December 2022 was conducted. Breathlessness was assessed using the Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnoea scale, derived from clinic letters pre-operatively and at routine post-operative follow-up. Pre- and post-operative MRC scores were compared using paired non-parametric testing. Secondary outcomes included post-operative complications, 30-day readmission and 30- and 90-day mortality. results: There were 37 patients identified who underwent diaphragm plication during the study period. Paired pre- and postoperative MRC scores were available for 32 patients. Median pre-operative MRC score was three (interquartile range [IQR] 3–4), improving to two (IQR 1–2) post-operatively, representing a median improvement of two MRC grades (p<0.001). Breathlessness improved in 31/32 patients (97%), was unchanged in 1/32 (3%) and worsened in none. Post-operative pneumonia occurred in three out of 37 patients (8%), and eight of 37 patients (22%) were readmitted within 30 days. There was no mortality at 30 or 90 days. conclusion: Diaphragm plication was associated with substantial improvement in patient-reported breathlessness and acceptable short-term morbidity in selected symptomatic patients.

title: A ( t , n )-threshold dynamic quantum secret sharing scheme based on two-particle quantum states
abstractText: Abstract Quantum secret sharing is an important branch of quantum cryptography. In this paper, we propose a ( t , n )-threshold dynamic quantum secret sharing scheme based on two-particle quantum states. By combining Shamir’s polynomial structure with sequential quantum operations, any t authorized participants can jointly reconstruct the shared secret, while fewer than t participants cannot obtain useful information. In the recovery phase, the weighted shares of the authorized participants are successively encoded into a transmitted two-particle quantum state, and random numbers are introduced to protect the intermediate quantum information. Moreover, the proposed scheme supports participant addition and deletion without changing the original secret. A new participant can obtain a valid share with the cooperation of an authorized subset, whereas the old shares of deleted participants are invalidated by refreshing the sharing polynomial. The correctness analysis shows that the secret can be accurately recovered by an authorized subset. The security analysis addresses selected attacks under the stated assumptions, but does not establish integrity protection against active state modification. Therefore, the proposed scheme achieves flexible threshold reconstruction and dynamic participant management based on two-particle quantum states.

title: Regulation of endogenous dsRNA: strategies for self-tolerance
abstractText: Abstract Cells must continuously distinguish cellular-derived RNA from pathogenic RNA to mount effective antiviral responses while avoiding harmful autoinflammation. Cytoplasmic RNA-sensing receptors, including RIG-I-like receptors, PKR, OAS-RNase L and ZBP1, detect RNA primarily through molecular features such as structure (double- versus single-stranded), modification state and subcellular localization rather than sequence. While these are characteristics of viral nucleic acids, mammalian genomes generate abundant self-derived double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), including from transposable elements, antisense transcription and RNA processing intermediates, which exist in the cytoplasm. This review describes our current understanding of how cells achieve self-tolerance through the active regulation of endogenous RNA. These mechanisms comprise epigenetic silencing of repetitive elements, RNA modifications (such as A-to-I editing and m6A), precise splicing, regulated nuclear export and decay, circRNA buffering, protein shielding and dedicated RNA degradation pathways. Insights from rare inherited monogenic interferonopathies and murine models illustrate how perturbations in these pathways lead to inappropriate activation of cytoplasmic RNA sensors and inflammatory disease when cellular dsRNA is mistakenly recognized as non-self. We highlight how dysregulated dsRNA homeostasis contributes to common autoimmune and neuroinflammatory disorders. Understanding how cells regulate endogenous dsRNA is crucial for defining disease mechanisms and developing new therapeutic strategies.

title: A multi-class anomaly signal classification method for fixed-point deformation combining PSO–VMD multiscale adaptive sample entropy and ALO–SOM model
abstractText: To address the challenge of identifying five predefined categories of disturbance-related abnormal signals (lightning interference, artificial blasting, power-supply failure, collapse-related events, and meteorological anomalies) in fixed-point deformation monitoring, this paper proposes an identification framework integrating parameter-optimized variational mode decomposition (VMD), multiscale entropy analysis, and an intelligent classification model. Firstly, particle swarm optimization is adopted to adaptively determine the mode number and penalty factor for VMD to realize adaptive signal decomposition. Then, an adaptive sample entropy algorithm with self-adjustable similarity thresholds is applied to extract multiscale complexity-oriented features from each decomposed modal component. Finally, the ant lion optimizer optimizes the competitive-layer topology and training hyperparameters of a self-organizing map network to build the target classifier. Comparative experiments against 18 widely-used classification models (including AdaBoost ensemble learners, generalized regression neural networks, long short-term memory networks, and gated recurrent units) are carried out on the real-world observation dataset from the Yixian seismic station. The experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive classification performance for the five anomaly categories. The mean test-set accuracy over 100 independent repeated-run experiments reaches 99.62%, with a standard deviation of 0.6361. This study offers an effective technical reference for identifying deformation-related abnormal waveforms under complex observational conditions.

title: Spatial and chemical heterogeneity of insect cuticular hydrocarbon layers: insights from extraction methods and acclimatization regimes
abstractText: Abstract Insect cuticles are covered by a complex mixture of cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) that are essential for desiccation resistance and chemical communication, yet the physical structure of CHC layers remains poorly understood. We extracted CHCs from five insect species (desert locusts, house crickets, American cockroaches and two ant species) using solvents of differing polarity and extraction durations, and from insects reared under different temperature regimes. Extractions with n-hexane were enriched in relatively solid CHCs (n-alkanes and terminally branched monomethylalkanes), while extractions with dichloromethane and dichloromethane–methanol yielded proportionally more fluid compounds (internally branched monomethyl and dimethylalkanes, unsaturated hydrocarbons). Solid-phase CHCs were proportionally more abundant in shorter extractions, whereas fluid-phase compounds were proportionally more abundant in prolonged or sequential extractions. These patterns are consistent with a model of cohesive solid domains surrounded by more accessible fluid regions, though this interpretation remains indirect and alternative explanations (e.g. differential solubility and diffusion kinetics) cannot be excluded. CHCs of similar phase behaviour covaried across treatments, indicating that they aggregate within shared domains. Warm acclimatization increased the proportion of solid compounds, whereas fluctuating temperatures enhanced CHCs with intermediate phase behaviour. Our results suggest spatial and chemical heterogeneity in the CHC layer, with patterns of differential extractability consistent with clustering into phase-distinct domains, though direct imaging is required to confirm spatial topology. This potential heterogeneity may facilitate CHC multi-functionality, with the phase behaviour and domain membership of each CHC depending on its biophysical properties relative to the individual's overall CHC profile.

title: Electronic-instability-driven phase separation enables grain-boundary toughening in high-entropy carbides
abstractText: Abstract High-entropy carbides (HECs) can exhibit enhanced phase stability, although elemental segregation and phase separation may occur under certain conditions. However, how intrinsic phase instability evolves under high pressure and how it can be exploited to regulate mechanical properties remain insufficiently understood. Here, (Hf(1−X)/4Zr(1−X)/4Nb(1−X)/4Ta(1−X)/4CoX)C (X = 0.14, 0.18, and 0.20) was investigated by integrating first-principles calculations with high-pressure sintering. The decomposition Gibbs free energy remains negative from 0 to 6 GPa, indicating an intrinsic thermodynamic driving force for Co segregation. Electronic-structure analysis reveals that pressure amplifies the bonding asymmetry between the stable transition-metal–C framework and the comparatively weaker Co–C interactions, as evidenced by the opposite pressure-dependence change in their integrated crystal orbital Hamiltonian population values. This bonding asymmetry is accompanied by local structural rearrangement, with the first Co–Co radial distribution function (RDF) peak shifting from 3.14 to 3.10 Å and increasing in intensity from 15.97 to 24.50. Experimentally, Co segregates into a ductile FCC phase preferentially distributed along grain boundaries, accompanied by an increase in the low-angle grain boundary fraction from 20.2% to 37.9%, indicating a possible contribution to local strain accommodation. The resulting heterogeneous microstructure facilitates crack deflection and branching, leading to an increase in fracture toughness from 4.5 ± 0.2 to 5.0 ± 0.2 MPa·m1/2. These findings demonstrate that pressure-driven electronic instability can be exploited to transform intrinsic phase instability into beneficial microstructural heterogeneity, providing a new strategy for toughening high-entropy ceramics.

title: PERANCANGAN ANTENA MIKROSTRIP LOG PERIODIC DIPOLE ARRAY (MLPDA) UNTUK SISTEM KOMUNIKASI LORA PADA FREKUENSI 920–923 MHZ
abstractText: Perkembangan Internet of Things meningkatkan kebutuhan terhadap teknologi komunikasi nirkabel yang mampu menyediakan jangkauan luas, konsumsi daya rendah, dan biaya implementasi yang relatif murah. Long Range (LoRa) merupakan salah satu teknologi yang memenuhi kebutuhan tersebut karena mampu mendukung transmisi jarak jauh dengan konsumsi daya rendah, dan di Indonesia beroperasi pada pita frekuensi 920–923 MHz. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang, merealisasikan, dan mengevaluasi antena Microstrip Log Periodic Dipole Array (MLPDA) enam elemen sebagai alternatif antena bawaan perangkat LoRa. Antena dirancang menggunakan substrat FR-4 Epoxy dengan konstanta dielektrik 4,3 dan ketebalan 1,6 mm. Tahapan penelitian meliputi perhitungan dimensi, pemodelan dan optimasi menggunakan CST Studio Suite 2019, fabrikasi, pengukuran menggunakan Vector Network Analyzer (VNA), serta pengujian pada perangkat LoRa. Pada frekuensi 920 MHz, 921,5 MHz, dan 923 MHz, nilai return loss hasil simulasi berturut-turut sebesar −13,65 dB, −13,77 dB, dan −13,90 dB, sedangkan hasil pengukuran masing-masing sekitar −16,70 dB, −17,00 dB, dan −17,30 dB. Nilai VSWR hasil simulasi pada ketiga frekuensi tersebut berturut-turut 1,52, 1,52, dan 1,51, sedangkan hasil pengukuran sebesar 1,34, 1,33, dan 1,32. Gain hasil simulasi masing-masing sebesar 3,347 dBi, 3,345 dBi, dan 3,342 dBi dengan pola radiasi directional dan polarisasi linear. Pengujian implementasi pada jarak 10 m, 20 m, dan 30 m menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan antena MLPDA pada sisi node dan hub meningkatkan nilai RSSI sebesar 7,33–13 dB dibandingkan antena bawaan. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa antena MLPDA yang dirancang memenuhi karakteristik kerja pada pita 920–923 MHz dan mampu meningkatkan kekuatan sinyal yang diterima pada sistem komunikasi LoRa.

title: Deficit discourse in health research in Aotearoa New Zealand: a medical student’s case for strengths-based and Kaupapa Māori approaches
abstractText: aim: The aim of this viewpoint was to examine how deficit discourse shapes health research and clinical practice in Aotearoa New Zealand and to argue that strengths-based framing and Kaupapa Māori methodologies should become standard expectations for researchers, clinicians, institutions and journals. method: A viewpoint was developed from the creation of an online module on strengths-based language for a Māori Health Advancement research curriculum, drawing on Kaupapa Māori scholarship and national and international evidence on the effects of deficit framing. results: Deficit framing remains routine in research, clinical documentation and quality improvement activity in Aotearoa. It obscures the structural determinants of inequity, transmits stigma between clinicians and reduces engagement with health services. Strengthsbased frames and Kaupapa Māori methodologies provide practical, evidence-informed alternatives, and specific responsibilities can be identified at each level of the research and health system. conclusion: The language of health research is an equity issue. Researchers, clinicians, institutions and journals in Aotearoa each hold distinct responsibilities to replace deficit discourse with mana-enhancing practice.

title: Foreword
abstractText: J. Michael Lennon recounts how Phillip Sipiora founded The Mailer Review with no paid staff, budget, or office: securing the partnership of the Norman Mailer Society and the University of South Florida with Mailer’s own blessing, recruiting and training a volunteer staff, and enriching the journal with unpublished and hard-to-find work by Mailer and with his own long interviews. Lennon judges the fifteen volumes Sipiora edited, with the Mailer collections at the Harry Ransom Center and Wilkes University, among the most important repositories of Mailer documents and commentary.

title: Strategi Indonesia dalam Mengurangi Angka Kematian Ibu
abstractText: Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) in Indonesia remains a major challenge in achieving national and global health development targets, particularly the targets of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This study aims to explore the various strategies implemented by the Indonesian government to reduce maternal mortality (AKI). The reduction of AKI is one of the sustainable development targets to be achieved by 2030. Several policies involving community empowerment, increasing access to health services, and health worker training have been implemented to improve the quality of maternal and antenatal care. The method used in this research is a literature review, analyzing various relevant journals and research reports. The results show that policies involving collaboration between the government, the community, and medical personnel have a positive impact on reducing maternal mortality (Darungan, 2020).

title: Beyond sperm competition: perspectives on sperm economy from external fertilizing fishes
abstractText: Abstract Research on sperm economy has traditionally focused on sperm competition as a major selective pressure shaping sperm production and allocation. In this review, we broaden this perspective by considering how other reproductive and ecological pressures influence the management of a costly and finite sperm supply. We synthesize evidence showing that in externally fertilizing fishes, high mating frequency, low female fecundity, prolonged spawning, rapid sperm dilution and costly male reproductive investment can favour sperm-economy strategies even when sperm competition is weak or absent. Across fish taxa, these constraints have led to convergent behavioural and physiological adaptations, including fractionated ejaculation, temporal matching of sperm release to egg deposition and manipulation of the fertilization microenvironment, which improve fertilization efficiency while minimizing sperm expenditure. We further highlight a recurring association between these strategies and semi-cystic spermatogenesis, consistent with the possibility that optimization of sperm use extends beyond ejaculate allocation to the regulation of sperm production during spermatogenesis. By integrating evidence from behaviour to reproductive physiology, this review reframes sperm economy as a general resource-allocation problem, with sperm competition representing one of several selective pressures. Externally fertilizing fishes emerge as an exceptional model for understanding the diverse evolutionary routes by which males optimize reproductive investment.

title: “It Might Not Be Unpleasant to Live”
abstractText: Mailer’s conviction to become a “psychic outlaw” has its genesis in his negative experience publishing The Deer Park, but his thoughts were leaning in this direction even before: specifically in his transitional short fiction that acts as a proving ground for ideas he workshopped in Lipton’s Journal and published in Advertisements for Myself—specifically in “The White Negro.” The group of short stories dating from the winter of 1951–52 allowed Mailer a space to explore the subversive ideas that would characterize his work after Advertisements for Myself.

Intrinsic noise reduces fluctuation frequencies in a cross-repressilator model motivated by stem cell differentiation
abstractText: Abstract The dynamical effects of intrinsic noise in gene regulatory networks (GRNs) can be significant when the number of molecules is low. In previous work, we proposed a new conceptual model, comprising a network of three transcription factors (TFs) that mutually inhibit each other (i.e. a ‘cross-repressilator’, also referred to as a ‘toggle triad’), that offers a route to reconcile the direct fate restriction (DFR) and progressive fate restriction (PFR) hypotheses for stem cell fate choice. In the deterministic case, the cross-repressilator model generically displays three kinds of dynamics. Between the multipotent and fate-specified regimes there exists a third, initially unanticipated, intermediate oscillatory regime that provides a mechanism for environmental signals to influence fate choice. Here, we analyse in detail a stochastic version of the cross-repressilator model. Our findings reveal that, as the system size reduces, intrinsic noise systematically lowers the characteristic frequencies associated with fluctuations both in the multipotent state and in the oscillatory regime. Hence, while the cross-repressilator conceptual model points to a possible resolution of the DFR/PFR dichotomy, the effect of noise is to reduce the number of oscillatory cycles that would be present and thus to accelerate movement of the cell state towards differentiation during the fate specification process.

title: Design principles for natural SGLT2 modulators from multi-scale computation
abstractText: Abstract Human sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (hSGLT2) is a membrane-embedded renal transporter and an established therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes. Hyperoside, myricetin, cyanidin-3-O-glucoside and isoliquiritigenin were investigated as a chemically diverse panel of natural scaffolds using a multi-scale computational workflow combining redocking-validated molecular docking, reconstruction of an unresolved transporter segment, molecular dynamics (MD) in an explicit POPC bilayer, molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, principal component and free-energy landscape analyses and density functional theory (DFT). The membrane simulations preserved the global hSGLT2 fold while revealing distinct ligand-dependent binding behaviours. Myricetin and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside exhibited limited positional deviations; hyperoside achieved persistent accommodation following an initial adjustment, whereas isoliquiritigenin underwent a marked late rearrangement. Ensemble-based energetic analysis prioritized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside, while hyperoside and myricetin formed an energetically comparable intermediate group and isoliquiritigenin displayed the least favourable profile. Electronic-structure analysis further characterized cyanidin-3-O-glucoside as the most responsive ligand within the DFT subset. Collectively, these findings indicate that glycone-assisted polar anchoring, aromatic complementarity and restricted conformational flexibility promote persistent hSGLT2 recognition. Direct hSGLT2 inhibition and hSGLT1 counter-screening assays remain necessary to establish potency and selectivity.

title: Prioritizing Impact: Cancers for Nanomedicine
abstractText: Abstract From the vantage point of the oncology clinic, the barriers keeping promising nanomedicines from patients look different than they appear from the research bench. Despite decades of preclinical progress, few patients are treated with nanoparticle-based therapies. This gap has two sides: well-characterized scientific obstacles, and a less-discussed set of clinical barriers that even a high-performing nanomedicine must overcome. In this Perspective, written from the viewpoint of a practicing oncologist, I argue that patient-centered design can mitigate some of these barriers and identify new opportunities for nanomedicine. I outline four principles that prioritize clinical impact: synergizing with the standard of care, advancing immuno-oncology combinations, embracing rare cancers, and improving supportive care. Bridging this gap will require clinicians, engineers, life and physical scientists, and industry partners to work together and adopt shared principles that put patients first.

title: Teaching Controversy
abstractText: Norman Mailer worked to change definitions of obscenity in his writing and the brash controversies of his writing makes him an especially compelling figure for the college classroom. Teaching provocative works by Mailer encourages students to see how controversies change over time and how their authors are celebrated and censored, often in direct response to these changes. One reason that Mailer works well in a college classroom is that he challenges his readers to move beyond rigid definitions of the moral and aesthetic. Mailer demands from his readers a marked distance and suspension of judgment in order to see what surface vulgarity can often obscure. This necessary distancing encourages students to make their own decisions about the relevance (or irrelevance) of obscenity charges to a text as a whole.

title: Unrecognized importance of hawking prey capture tactics in a tropical plunge-diving seabird
abstractText: Abstract Seabirds are critical ecosystem members providing connectivity between marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Seabird foraging is often facilitated by other marine predators (e.g. tuna) that aggregate prey at the surface. Some seabirds have been anecdotally reported to ‘hawk’ (catch mid-air/in-flight) flyingfish and flying squid forced into flight by subsurface predators. Hawking avoids water entry and subsequent take-off, both of which are known to be energy intensive, but its relative importance in foraging has not been quantified. We analysed footage from 25 animal-borne video cameras deployed on red-footed boobies (Sula sula) at Palmyra Atoll to estimate the frequency of hawking, plunge diving and ‘other’ prey capture attempts. Hawking made up 20.3% of all prey capture attempts and had a 39.3% success rate in 2022, but was not observed for the two tracked birds in 2024. An additional 17 individuals were opportunistically observed in the footage making hawking capture attempts, suggesting hawking is a common behaviour, accounting for a greater proportion of foraging effort than previously known. As hawking is only possible when subsurface predators elicit flight escape behaviours of prey, its high frequency suggests such predator facilitation interactions are stronger than currently understood.

title: INTEGRATED LABORATORY ADMINISTRATION SYSTEM BERBASIS QR CODE DAN GOOGLE APPS SCRIPT
abstractText: Administrasi laboratorium pada institusi pendidikan tinggi sering kali menghadapi kendala keterlambatan informasi, ketidakakuratan data inventaris, dan tingginya ketergantungan pada dokumen berbasis kertas akibat pengelolaan manual yang terfragmentasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang, membangun, dan mengimplementasikan Integrated Laboratory Administration System berbasis Quick Response (QR) Code dan Google Apps Script (GAS). Sistem ini dirancang untuk mengintegrasikan alur kerja pengelolaan ruangan, inventarisasi alat, penggunaan bahan habis pakai, pemantauan SOP digital, serta pembuatan dokumen administrasi praktikum secara otomatis. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah Research and Development (R&D) dengan pendekatan System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model Waterfall yang mencakup analisis kebutuhan, perancangan arsitektur, pengembangan sistem, implementasi QR Code, pengujian, dan evaluasi. Sistem dikembangkan memanfaatkan ekosistem cloud Google Workspace (Google Form, Google Sheets, Google Docs, dan Google Drive) tanpa memerlukan infrastruktur server fisik tambahan. QR Code diterapkan sebagai jembatan Physical-to-Digital pada objek fisik laboratorium. Hasil pengujian fungsi menggunakan Black Box Testing menunjukkan tingkat keberhasilan fungsi $\ge 90\%$, sedangkan evaluasi User Acceptance Test (UAT) menghasilkan tingkat kepuasan pengguna sebesar $88.5\%$. Penggunaan sistem ini mampu mempercepat pembuatan laporan PDF otomatis menjadi ratarata 38 detik, mengurangi waktu administrasi sebesar 65%, serta menurunkan pemakaian kertas hingga 82%. Penelitian ini terbukti efektif dalam mendukung tata kelola laboratorium yang modern, efisien, dan mendukung konsep Zero-Paper Laboratory Administration

title: A theory for designing capillary systems of constant interaction
abstractText: Abstract The attraction or repulsion force between two solid objects at a liquid-gas interface (i.e. the lateral capillary interaction force) is generally considered to be highly dependent on both the shapes of the solid surfaces and the relative positions. To challenge this, we propose an exotic capillary system in which the stationary exotic plate piercing the interface can produce a constant capillary interaction force on a partly immersed cylinder at different horizontal positions. This constancy is owing to the counterbalancing of variations in the horizontal components of the surface tension force and the hydrostatic pressure force on the cylinder. Through analysing the meniscus profiles and the capillary interaction force in the proposed exotic capillary system, five types of exotic plate shapes are identified. More importantly, a further analysis indicates that the lateral capillary interaction force in the proposed exotic capillary system remains constant even for different vertical positions of the cylinder. To verify the practicality of our theory, a three-dimensional numerical investigation is conducted, and the results show that the lateral capillary interaction force can remain nearly constant as expected. The proposed capillary system provides new insight into controlling the capillary interaction force. The constant-force regimes suggest passive routes for interfacial transport and micromanipulation, force regulation and suppression of undesired capillary aggregation.

title: Mono- and Bis-NHC Ruthenium Complexes─Theoretical Insights into Stability and Ligand Exchange Selectivity
abstractText: Abstract Ruthenium–N-heterocyclic carbene complexes used as catalysts for olefin metathesis may exist as either mono-NHC or bis-NHC species. We used a number of computational methods, ranging from semiempirical and DFT approaches to highly accurate symmetry-adapted perturbation theory (SAPT) approaches to determine which of the electronic and structural features are accountable for the formation and the stability of the final catalyst. We found that modern DFT functionals accurately describe the formation of the majority of ruthenium complexes and correctly identify the most stable rotamer, while other approaches combining GFN2-xTB and DFT or SAPT methods give accurate geometries but inaccurate energies. We also showed that the calculated bond dissociation energies of ligands and intramolecular interactions between substituents may serve as computationally less expensive metrics for the estimation of the stability of ruthenium complexes. Finally, we also analyzed the influence of electronic and steric effects on the stability of studied complexes.

title: When Learning Becomes a Game: The Impact of Ladders War in Game-Based Learning on Students' Mathematical Critical Thinking Skills
abstractText: Mathematical critical thinking remains a persistent challenge in elementary education globally, as TIMSS 2023 findings show that only a small proportion of fourth-grade students worldwide reached the High and Advanced benchmarks in mathematics, while empirical evidence on the effectiveness of game-based approaches at the primary level remains limited. This study examined how the Game-Based Learning (GBL) model, assisted by Ladders War media, influenced fourth-grade students' mathematical critical-thinking skills in number patterns, a topic fundamental to algebraic reasoning that remains persistently difficult for young learners. Employing a quasi-experimental Nonequivalent Control Group Design, 50 students (aged 9–10; 25 males, 25 females) from two intact classes in Bekasi, Indonesia, participated. The study was conducted over four 90-minute sessions: the pretest was administered at the beginning of the first session, followed by the first treatment, two additional treatment sessions, and a posttest in the fourth session. Critical thinking was assessed using a five-item expert-validated essay test (reliability = 0.74) measuring analysis, inference, evaluation, and explanation. ANCOVA with pretest scores as the covariate yielded a large effect size (η²p = 0.217) and a significant between-group difference (F = 13.013, p < .001), with an adjusted mean difference of 13.132 points (95% CI [5.809, 20.455]). The GBL group achieved a higher learning gain (N-Gain = 0.56, moderate) than the control group (N-Gain = 0.33, moderate). These findings suggest that the GBL model with Ladders War media effectively supports the development of mathematical critical thinking among elementary school students. Theoretically, this study reinforces the use of GBL to foster higher-order thinking, while practically offering an innovative instructional alternative for mathematics teachers, with broader implications for mathematics education in developing-country contexts. Keywords: game-based learning, mathematical critical thinking, ladders war.

title: Connecting Conformational Landscapes with Bioactivity in Macrocyclic Kinase Inhibitors
abstractText: Abstract Macrocyclization can improve the selectivity and pharmacokinetic properties of kinase inhibitors, yet the conformational basis of these effects remains incompletely understood. Here, we characterized the structures and conformational ensembles of the clinically relevant macrocyclic kinase inhibitors pacritinib and zotiraciclib using microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED), NMR spectroscopy, and molecular docking. Both compounds populate a set of related macrocyclic core conformations, with additional conformational adaptability arising from changes in aromatic torsion angles and substituent orientations. These conformational adaptations correlate with physicochemical properties relevant to aqueous solubility and membrane permeability. Pacritinib exhibits chameleonic behavior through environment-dependent modulation of its exposed polar surface area, whereas protonation of zotiraciclib generates distinct conformational states stabilized by intramolecular cation–π interactions. Molecular docking indicates that the experimentally determined conformations are compatible with productive binding across multiple kinase targets. Collectively, these findings establish a link between conformational adaptability, physicochemical properties, and polypharmacology in macrocyclic kinase inhibitors, providing insights that may guide the rational design of future macrocyclic therapeutics.

title: The repeated evolution of anti-bat bioacoustics in hawkmoths
abstractText: Abstract Predator–prey interactions impose strong selective forces, often resulting in remarkable anti-predatory adaptations. Among insects, moths have been engaged in a long-standing arms race with bats, leading to the evolution of diverse anti-predator strategies. Here, we investigate the evolution of anti-bat stridulatory behaviour in hawkmoths (Lepidoptera: Sphingidae) by integrating acoustic recordings, high-resolution scanning electron microscopy and micro-computed tomography imaging and a time-calibrated phylogeny. We classify three distinct ultrasound-producing systems—scale-on-scale, scale-on-spine and scale-on-nodule—based on the interaction of scraper and file components. Building on previous descriptions, we uncover new details of two stridulatory mechanisms and describe for the first time the file component in the scale-on-nodule system of Macroglossinae. Phylogenetic analyses reveal that stridulatory responses to bat echolocation evolved independently multiple times among hawkmoths within the past approximately 30 million years. Furthermore, we demonstrate that divergent lineages produce acoustically distinct signals that correlate with variation in stridulatory morphology and the presence or absence of hearing organs. Collectively, our results highlight the repeated evolution of ultrasonic defences across divergent hawkmoth lineages and underscore predator–prey conflict as a powerful driver of both evolutionary innovation and redundancy in bioacoustic warfare.

title: Complications in Pediatric Cancer Patients With Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infection
abstractText: BACKGROUND Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (BSIs) can cause significant morbidity in children with cancer. Current guidelines recommend central venous catheter (CVC) removal, though the necessity remains uncertain. We assessed risk factors for complications among affected patients, focusing on impact of CVC removal vs salvage. METHODS This multicenter retrospective study includes pediatric oncology patients with S aureus BSIs from 2005 to 2022. The complication outcome period (72 hours to 6 months after initial positive culture) was divided into short-term (72 hours to 8 days) and late periods (8 days to 6 months). The composite primary outcome included occurrence of at least 1 major complication: recurrent BSIs, deep abscess/myositis, S aureus–related death, exit site infection, meningitis, endocarditis, or osteomyelitis. Multivariable logistic regression with propensity score weighting for CVC removal was performed. RESULTS Among 322 BSI episodes, 90.7% (n = 292/322) had a CVC at presentation; salvage was attempted in 55.5% (n = 162/292). The primary outcome was met in 21.2% (n = 62/292) of episodes with a CVC, more frequently in the CVC salvage (25.3%, n = 41/161) vs removal (16.2%, n = 21/130) group. CVC salvage was independently associated with the primary outcome (OR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.08–5.61; P < .01) in short-term (OR, 21.8; 95% CI, 7.09–95.4) and late (OR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.06–3.18) periods. Methicillin resistance, male sex, invasive infection at presentation, implanted ports, sepsis, and persistent blood culture positivity were also independently associated with the primary outcome. CONCLUSIONS CVC removal was associated with fewer short-term and late complications in pediatric cancer patients with S aureus BSIs, supporting recommendations for catheter removal in this population.

Foot-stiffening socks reduce the metabolic cost of walking
abstractText: Abstract Greater foot longitudinal bending stiffness theoretically facilitates bipedal walking by reducing whole-body metabolic rate, yet empirical evidence is elusive. Here, we tested this theory by studying human walking with and without foot-stiffening socks. These custom socks applied more pressure to the user's forefoot than commercially available socks (p < 0.001), which in turn increased medial longitudinal arch stiffness through cross-axis coupling (p = 0.034). Walking with foot-stiffening socks reduced whole-body metabolic rate 2% versus the use of commercial socks (p = 0.008). Biomechanically, stiffening participants' feet increased ankle gear ratio (peak: p = 0.017; average: p = 0.045) and reduced the ankle's average angular velocity during the stance-phase of walking (p = 0.018). In congruence, leg muscle fascicle shortening velocities decreased 15–20% (soleus: p = 0.023; medial gastrocnemius: p = 0.005), contributing to the 9–12% reduction in estimated leg active muscle volume (model1: p = 0.015; model2: p = 0.142). Therefore, foot-stiffening socks make walking less effortful by eliciting more economical leg muscle contractions, supporting the notion that the evolved stiffening of human feet facilitate terrestrial bipedal locomotion.

Integrated multi-omics analysis deciphers the molecular mechanisms underlying the characteristic volatile flavor of Meishan pork
abstractText: Abstract Background The Meishan pig is a celebrated indigenous Chinese swine breed renowned for its distinctive flavor profile. However, the specific signature flavor compounds and the molecular mechanisms underlying their formation remain largely uncharacterized. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the volatile flavor compounds across five pig breeds and decipher the molecular basis of the characteristic flavor of Meishan pork. Results Comparative analysis combining electronic nose, headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), and relative odor activity value calculations revealed that Meishan pork contained significantly higher levels of four key aroma compounds: hexanal, nonanal, 2-pentylfuran, and (E,E)-2,4-nonadienal. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses identified oleic acid and α-linolenic acid as critical precursors and highlighted the high expression of the arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase gene ( ALOX5 ) in Meishan pigs. Heating experiments confirmed that these fatty acids yield characteristic flavor compounds upon thermal oxidation. Furthermore, functional studies demonstrated that ALOX5 catalyzes the conversion of these precursors into flavor aldehydes. Conclusions The distinctive flavor of Meishan pork is associated with a dual mechanism: thermal oxidation of abundant precursors during cooking, and enhanced enzymatic oxidation prior to cooking resulting from constitutively high ALOX5 expression. By deciphering the flavor formation mechanism from metabolic precursors to enzyme-catalyzed conversion, this investigation provides a framework for elucidating meat flavor chemistry and offers potential targets for breeding strategies aimed at improving pork flavor.
