title: KARAKTERISASI EKSPERIMENTAL TERMINATOR RF BERBASIS ABSORBER SEKAM PADI BAKAR PADA RENTANG FREKUENSI 2–7,5 GHz
abstractText: This study experimentally characterizes a radio-frequency (RF) terminator using burned rice husk as an absorber over 2–7.5 GHz. The terminator was constructed from a 50 mm × 30 mm × 30 mm hollow-steel casing with a SubMiniature version A (SMA) connector mounted on the front surface, while burned rice husk powder was poured directly into the internal cavity. According to the laboratory test report, the black rice-husk ash sample used in the study had a reported carbon content of 48% and a moisture content of 4.2%. Measurements were performed using a SIGLENT SVA1075X after one-port Open–Short–Load calibration. The operating criterion was defined as voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) ≤ 2, equivalent to S11 ≤ −9.54 dB. The VNA documentation showed S11 = −9.42 dB at 3.17722 GHz. Because numerical sweep data were not retained, the threshold crossing was not interpolated and the lower operating boundary is conservatively reported at approximately 3.18 GHz. The lowest documented S11 was −50.74 dB at 5.377165 GHz, corresponding to a VSWR of approximately 1.006. At 7.4903 GHz, S11 remained −30.73 dB, and the response continued to satisfy the criterion up to the 7.5 GHz instrument limit. Thus, the observed operating range extends from approximately 3.18 GHz to at least 7.5 GHz, corresponding to a frequency span of ≥4.32 GHz within the measurement window. The result indicates the potential of a burned-rice-husk-filled one-port terminator for wide-range RF termination, while the measured response represents the complete device rather than the intrinsic absorber properties alone.

title: A Critical Analysis of Sociology Teachers' Pedagogical Practices Through Performance Test Documents of the 2025 In-Service Teacher Professional Education Program
abstractText: This study aims to (1) describe the completeness and alignment of lesson planning in the teaching modules of Sociology teachers who took the 2025 In-Service Teacher UKIN with the indications of learning practice they contain, viewed through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and (2) critically analyze teacher performance in the UKIN through the critical pedagogy perspectives of Paulo Freire and Henry Giroux and Stephen Ball's theory of performativity. The study used a qualitative approach, applying Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis to a purposive sample of 190 Sociology teaching-module documents from UKIN participants at one teacher-education institution (LPTK). The results show that the administrative-format completeness of the teaching modules is generally good, while the substantive depth of teachers' pedagogical competence remains variable. Lesson planning tends to target low-to-moderate cognitive levels, with lower-order thinking categories dominating most modules; assessment items misalign with Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS)-oriented learning objectives in most documents; and PowerPoint remains the dominant, often the only, technology used across most modules. Viewed through the critical lenses of Freire's banking education, Giroux's transformative intellectuals, and Ball's performativity theory, these findings suggest that the UKIN's current design and practice emphasize administrative and technical compliance more than cultivating substantive pedagogical reflection among teachers. Nevertheless, these patterns also reveal concrete entry points for reform, including rubric refinement, continuous mentoring, and reflective assessment components, through which the UKIN could more fully realize its intended role in fostering transformative, reflective teaching practice.Keywords: Teacher performance test; TPACK, Critical pedagogy, Sociology teaching module, Performativity

title: Analisis Pemahaman Siswa kelas IV MI tentang Dampak Pembuangan Sampah terhadap Keseimbangan Ekosistem
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pemahaman siswa kelas IV Madrasah Ibtidaiyah mengenai dampak pembuangan sampah terhadap keseimbangan ekosistem. Fokus penelitian meliputi kemampuan siswa dalam membedakan jenis sampah, menjelaskan dampak pencemaran terhadap lingkungan, memahami hubungan sebab-akibat antara pembuangan sampah dan kehidupan organisme, serta mengaitkan konsep ekosistem dengan kehidupan sehari-hari. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif dengan metode campuran (mixed methods) yang memadukan data kualitatif dan kuantitatif. Penelitian dilaksanakan di Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Nurul Islam 1 dengan melibatkan siswa kelas IV serta informan yang relevan dengan pelaksanaan pembelajaran. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara, angket, telaah dokumen, dan dokumentasi. Data dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña melalui kondensasi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi. Hasil penelitian akan digunakan untuk menggambarkan aspek pemahaman siswa yang telah dikuasai dan aspek yang masih memerlukan penguatan dalam memahami keterkaitan antara pembuangan sampah, pencemaran lingkungan, dan keseimbangan ekosistem.

title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates
abstractText: Abstract Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. We quantify the causal effects of taxonomy, extinction risk, accessibility (range size, depth, economic context, year of description) and charisma (body size, shape, patterning and colouration) on species-level research outputs from more than 7000 publications. Research effort was strongly taxonomically biased, driven by accessibility and charisma, with shallow depth, broad geographic ranges, large body size and distinctive morphologies attracting disproportionate attention. Extinction risk exerted a counterintuitive nonlinear effect: Critically Endangered and Endangered species received significantly fewer publications than Near Threatened and Vulnerable species and were comparable to Data Deficient species. This effect is consistent with a ‘Goldilocks’ zone in which species are threatened enough to justify research but not so threatened that it becomes prohibitively challenging. Systematic research bias away from the species most in need undermines conservation efforts. Realigning research priorities is essential to combating the biodiversity crisis.

title: Ion Valence Difference Governs Membrane Charge Preference in Nanofiltration-Based Radionuclide Separation
abstractText: Abstract Selective separation of radionuclides with varying environmental hazards is critical for mitigating the disposal burden of high-level radioactive wastewater. Although positively charged (PC) membranes are generally considered effective for cation pair separation, the applicability of negatively charged (NC) membranes for separating cations with large valence differences remains unresolved. In this study, Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ were used as representative radionuclides with large and small valence differences, respectively, to evaluate the separation performance and underlying mechanisms of PC and NC membranes. Notably, NC membranes maintained near-complete rejection of Zr4+ while simultaneously exhibiting higher Ag+ permeability, thereby achieving superior Ag+/Zr4+ selectivity relative to PC membranes. DFT calculations and MD simulations revealed that strong ion–membrane interactions facilitated preferential partitioning of Zr4+ at the NC membrane interface, whereas differences in hydration energy governed the competitive transport of Ag+ and Zr4+. Furthermore, Zr4+ accumulated at the membrane surface induced incomplete dehydration of Ag+, reducing interfacial transport barriers and promoting Ag+ permeation. Comparative analysis of Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ systems further demonstrated that ion valence difference governs the preference of membrane charges: NC membranes are preferred for M+/M4+ separations, whereas PC membranes are preferred for M+/M2+ separations, which was further validated by Li+/Mg2+ and Li+/Ti4+ separations. These findings clarify the mechanistic distinction between co-ion and counterion competition, providing guidance for the selection of membrane charge types for energy-efficient radionuclide separation and selective resource recovery beyond the nuclear industry.

abstractText: Penanaman Modal Asing (PMA) merupakan salah satu instrumen penting dalam mendukung pertumbuhan ekonomi, penciptaan lapangan kerja, transfer teknologi, dan peningkatan produktivitas nasional. What drives the winter behaviour and ecology of the temperate coral Astrangia poculata? An examination of thermal and nutritional cues
abstractText: Abstract In temperate ecosystems, accessing subtidal environments in the winter is challenging, and therefore, winter ecology and seasonal variation are understudied. For the temperate coral Astrangia poculata, winter is thought to be a period of biological ‘reset’, in which many cellular processes slow or stop, and the microbiome and symbiont community shift dramatically. The period of quiescence, when corals enter a dormant state with limited feeding or metabolic activity, is primarily driven by cold temperatures. However, other ecological drivers of quiescence remain unclear. Here, we documented quiescence in symbiotic and aposymbiotic colonies of A. poculata over a four-month winter period at two depths. First, we confirmed that quiescence is strongly associated with water temperatures under 6°C. Although we quantified a thermocline associated with depth, there was no influence of depth on quiescence. Symbiotic corals were more likely than aposymbiotic corals to enter quiescence, and higher chlorophyll α concentration was associated with lower quiescence, indicating a nutritional link to quiescence in A. poculata. Finally, we compared our results with previous quiescence observations and determined that the dormancy period is shorter in warmer winters, which has implications for the future ecology and behaviour of A. poculata in an era of global change.

title: Sublethal insecticide exposure and inbreeding impose a developmental bottleneck but enhance crop-damaging traits in surviving Colorado potato beetles
abstractText: Abstract Intensive agricultural insecticide use often fails to eradicate pest populations completely, leaving small remnant populations exposed to persistent sublethal residues and potentially elevated inbreeding. How such remnant populations persist remains poorly understood. Here, we examined how inbreeding and sublethal imidacloprid exposure shape survival and post-emergence performance in the Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata), a major agricultural pest. We compared four groups differing in breeding status and insecticide exposure history, and quantified emergence rate, locomotor activity, feeding behaviour and reproductive output. We found that despite the insecticide dosage being sublethal, both chemical exposure and inbreeding imposed severe developmental costs, reducing the adult emergence rate with no significant interaction effects. However, among the adults, we observed trait-specific phenotypic plasticity. Male locomotor activity was reduced by both stressors, while female activity remained stable. Notably, herbivory significantly increased under both inbreeding and sublethal insecticide exposure. Furthermore, while inbreeding severely reduced both egg production and hatching success, sublethal exposure to the insecticide surprisingly increased hatching success in surviving pairs. These results demonstrate that sublethal insecticide exposure and inbreeding can create a strong developmental bottleneck. Yet, surviving individuals can exhibit compensatory plasticity that maintains or even enhances their capacity for crop damage.

title: Anomaly detection of asset data in power monitoring systems based on knowledge graph reasoning
abstractText: Abstract Edge computing nodes face severe constraints on both computing and storage resources, and the dynamic correlation of asset data remains complex within power monitoring systems. To address this challenge, this study proposes an anomaly detection framework that is based on knowledge graph reasoning and tailored for asset data in such systems. The framework first constructs a lightweight embedding method for knowledge graphs, then introduces a time-sliding window mechanism that builds a sequence of dynamic subgraphs, thereby adapting to the dynamic evolution of the network topology. Following this, the approach combines relational attribute modulation with low-rank matrix decomposition, thereby reducing both the model’s global parameter count and its memory overhead. It then proposes a relation-aware lightweight graph attention network. Within this network, a differential projection decoupling mechanism separates the coupling effects between target nodes and relational features. In addition, the approach introduces a sparse attention truncation selection strategy to filter out low-frequency background noise. Based on real datasets collected from substations and distribution networks, the results show that the proposed model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.982 on dataset A and an accuracy of 0.949 on dataset B. The low-rank matrix decomposition strategy reduced memory usage by 94.68 %, while the differential projection decoupling mechanism maintained a stable F1-score of 97.25 %. Furthermore, six months of continuous monitoring with the dynamic time-sliding window kept the F1-score stable at around 97 % and yielded an average alarm delay of only 0.8 s. These findings indicate that the proposed detection model effectively enhances the robustness of the power monitoring system against concept drift and network topology evolution, thereby providing technical support for lightweight intelligent monitoring and the safe deployment of edge devices for power assets.

Inevitable fates? The recovery potential of small populations
abstractText: Abstract The recovery prospects of species reduced to critically small numbers are frequently seen in a pessimistic light. Even if conservation efforts could successfully tackle drivers of severe decline, small population effects would be expected to inhibit population growth. Accounts of dramatic conservation recoveries seem to challenge this narrative, but without a broader examination encompassing all actions and outcomes, the representativeness of success stories alone is unclear. Here, we conduct an observational study evaluating all 147 bird and mammal species that have been below 50 individuals in the wild at any point since 1950, of which 141 had sufficient elapsed time to assess an outcome. We characterized the history, if any, of conservation action in these species, and used Bayesian multi-level logistic regression to model its association with subsequent population status. Most species subject to direct conservation recovered to at least 100 individuals, with the highest modelled recovery probabilities associated with those subject to a combination of actions to limit external drivers of decline and directly manipulate populations. These findings indicate a striking potential for recovery even in critically small populations and serve as an empirically grounded counterpoint to advocates of abandonment of such species under a conservation triage framework.

title: Evaluation of a Dye-Sensitized Solar Cell [DSSC] device based on Agaricus bisporus extract
abstractText: This study evaluates the photoelectrochemical performance of natural extracts from Agaricus bisporus [Portobello variety] as photosensitizers in dye-sensitized solar cells [DSSCs]. Photoanodes were prepared with mesoporous TiO2, and activated carbon counter electrodes were catalytic thermally activated. Photoelectric characterization under natural solar irradiance [930 W/m] demonstrated efficient charge injection promoted by DOPA-melanin chromophores. Prototypes achieved a maximum open-circuit voltage [Voc] of 34.2 mV, a fill factor [FF] of 0.454, and a overall power conversion efficiency [η] of 0.0374%. These results confirm the stability and technical feasibility of crude fungal biomass for sustainable optoelectronic devices, setting an experimental baseline for non-purified bio-sensitizers.

title: Vanishing sea ice threatens Southern Ocean isopod species diversity
abstractText: Abstract Sea-ice retreat is rapidly transforming the Southern Ocean (SO), yet consequences for benthic biodiversity remain poorly resolved. Here, we show that declining sea ice is directly linked to reduced species diversity in benthic isopods, a dominant SO fauna (Pearson's r = 0.56). We analysed 214 isopod species from 78 genera in the Atlantic sector using a 14-year dataset integrating satellite and in situ observations across 60–77° S and 403–4976 m depths. Of these 214 species, 32% (68) occur exclusively at high sea-ice stations, and among them 53% are new to science and 75% are rare. Redundancy analysis (variance explained 15.3% and 6.5% for axes 1 and 2; p ≤ 0.002) and generalized linear models (p = 0.0025) identify sea-ice cover as a primary driver of species richness (Pearson's r = 0.56) and community composition. Declining sea ice is associated with lower diversity and shifts in assemblage structure, indicating strong coupling between cryosphere change and deep-sea biodiversity. Given that the SO is a global biodiversity hotspot, these findings reveal unquantified vulnerability of seafloor communities. With continued sea-ice decline projected, irreversible biodiversity losses are likely, underscoring an urgent need for climate mitigation as impacts reach the farthest marine frontiers.

title: Analytical modal analysis of lumped stiffness-mass structures via a recursive static solution
abstractText: Abstract This paper examines the modal properties, including modal frequencies and mode shapes, of lumped stiffness-mass systems with one degree-of-freedom (dof) per node. For the first time, it attains recursive solutions for the modal properties of such structures with general configurations. To this end, we introduce a recursive formulation to construct the stiffness and mass matrices of structures, and transform modal analysis into equivalent static problems of ‘modified structures’, where the masses assume a role of negative-stiffness springs. The static analysis of these modified structures hinges on a family of recursive functions, named characteristic rational P-functions, which encode all modal properties of the original structures. This recursive static solution allows modal analysis with an algorithmic complexity linear to the total number of dofs. We further derive exact modal solutions for structures with uniform stiffness and mass. The analysis includes the dispersion of modal frequencies, the linearity of modal periods to structural heights, the spectral distribution and the geometrical interpretation of mode shapes. The cumulative distribution of modal frequencies exhibits a staircase shape that converges to inverse trigonometric functions for a sufficiently large number of dofs. Lastly, we validate the convergence of an infinite-dof discrete model to a continuum model.

title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2-Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method
abstractText: Abstract Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. Receptor flexibility was then introduced through the CorrEA protocol, which cross-docks the series against an ensemble of Lck conformations sampled by molecular dynamics (MD) and, using the measured activities of the series as a reference, selects for each ligand the receptor–pose pair that best accounts for the observed potencies. The resulting ensemble accommodated the entire compound set, overcoming the inability of the rigid receptor to host eight of the derivatives, while preserving the canonical orientation of the AHBA scaffold within the ATP-binding site. The ensemble also recovered the hinge and gatekeeper hydrogen bonds to M319 and T316 expected for ATP-competitive protein kinase (PK) inhibitors, which were only partially satisfied in the rigid-receptor poses. Examination of the selected conformations indicates that the series is accommodated through modest, coordinated rearrangements distributed across the glycine-rich loop, the region beyond the hinge, and the back pocket, rather than through a single dominant conformational change. These models offer an activity-consistent structural framework for interpreting ligand recognition by Lck and a transferable workflow for PKs whose binding sites are conformationally labile.

title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches
abstractText: Abstract Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔGML < −11 kcal mol−1. Molecular docking identified six top candidates with favorable binding affinities ranging from −5.856 to −9.667 kcal mol⁻¹, which subsequently underwent 200 ns MD simulations. Structural analyses confirmed the stability of all ALK–ligand complexes, while interaction studies revealed extensive hydrophobic contacts and conserved hydrogen bonds involving key ALK residues. US calculations estimated binding free energies from −8.354 to −13.272 kcal mol−1, with compound 54 exhibiting the strongest affinity (ΔGUS = −13.272 kcal mol−1). Several alkaloids, including acrifoline, heptazoline, and atalaphyllidine, also demonstrated promisingbinding properties and reported anticancer activities. Toxicity prediction indicated acceptable safety profiles, highlighting Glycosmis-derived phytochemicals as promising potential ALK inhibitor candidates and supporting the utility of ML-guided virtual screening combined with advanced molecular simulations for natural product-based anticancer drug discovery. Nevertheless, biochemical and cellular experiments are required to confirm their ALK inhibitory activity, selectivity, and therapeutic potential.

title: Incorporating authority perception, economic status and behavioural response in infectious disease control
abstractText: Abstract We introduce a multi-population mean field game framework to examine how economic status and authority perception shape vaccination and social distancing decisions under different epidemic control policies. We conducted a survey to inform our model and stratify the population into six groups by income and perception of authority, capturing behavioural heterogeneity. Individuals choose socialization and vaccination levels to optimize objectives such as minimizing treatment costs, complying with social distancing guidelines if they are authority-followers, or reducing losses from decreased social interactions if they are authority-indifferents, alongside economic costs. Public health authorities influence behaviour through social distancing guidelines and vaccination costs. We characterize the Nash equilibrium via a forward–backward differential equation system, provide its mathematical analysis and numerically solve it. Our findings reveal a trade-off between social distancing and vaccination. Under stricter guidelines that target both susceptible and infected individuals, followers reduce both socialization and vaccination levels, while indifferents increase socialization owing to followers’ preventative measures. Adaptive guidelines targeting infected individuals effectively reduce infections and narrow the gap between low- and high-income groups, while lower vaccination costs incentivize vaccination among low-income groups. Trust-building remains critical in epidemic mitigation, underscoring the importance of data-informed, game-theoretical models for understanding complex human responses to mitigation policies.

title: Reframing L2 Pragmatic Competence in the Generative AI Era: A Co-Design-Oriented Critical Curriculum
abstractText: The rapid incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into second-language (L2) education has reopened a foundational question in language pedagogy: what should count as successful communication when English is routinely used among speakers who do not share a native-speaker norm? Much L2 pragmatic instruction continues to treat pragmatics as the acquisition of socially appropriate forms modelled on idealised native-speaker practices. This conceptual review article proposes a co-design-oriented critical pragmatic curriculum that positions GAI (implemented primarily through large language models, or LLMs) not as an infallible tutor but as a contestable intercultural interlocutor. Drawing on English as a Lingua Franca (ELF), World Englishes, translanguaging, critical pragmatics, critical digital literacy, and design-based research (DBR), the paper advances a unified pedagogical architecture comprising three modules: Persona Engineering and Dialectic Diversity, Real-Time Meaning Negotiation, and Deconstructing Algorithmic Bias, each enacted through a four-stage learning episode (persona engineering → GAI interaction → critical negotiation → reflection and transfer) and organised within an iterative co-design cycle. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded model for integrating GAI with intercultural and critical language pedagogy while retaining teacher mediation, learner agency, multilingual resources, and ethical safeguards. It argues that the educational value of GAI lies less in making learners sound more native-like than in helping them become more observant, adaptive, critical, and strategically competent participants in multilingual communication.

title: Predictive modeling of color and sucrose in the cane sugar industry using key explanatory variables
abstractText: The most influential variables affecting two key sugar quality characteristics sucrose content [percentage of sucrose] and ICUMSA color were identified, along with predictive models for each characteristic. The objective of this study was to determine the sugar production variables that have the greatest impact on sucrose content [% pol] and sugar color [°ICUMSA], and subsequently to develop predictive models capable of simulating different scenarios to support effective decision-making. Principal Component Analysis [PCA] was employed to extract the variables with the greatest influence on each quality characteristic. Subsequently, multiple linear regression was applied using the variables selected through PCA. As a result, two predictive models were obtained: one explaining 100% of the variability in sucrose content and another explaining 98% of the variability in ICUMSA color. Both models will be used to induce process changes that ensure compliance with the product quality specifications required by national and international customers.

title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
abstractText: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. The as-synthesized Co-Mo2S3/carbon foam (CF) achieved an average evaporation rate of 2.13 kg m-2 h-1 during a 1-h experiment under 1,000 W m-2 irradiation using a 3.5% NaCl solution, compared to 1.55 kg m-2 h-1 obtained for CF. A Taguchi orthogonal-array design of experiments (DOE) was used to optimize the effect of input parameters on the evaporation rate of saline water. The experimental design matrix shows a maximum water evaporation rate of 1.77 kg m-2 h-1 under real sunlight. Taguchi analysis presents the optimal operating parameters for the evaporation rate as follows: salinity 30 g L-1 (level 1), saline water pH 5 (level 2), and time 2 h (level 2). The statistical outcomes show that salinity is the main factor affecting the evaporation rate. This study addresses water scarcity and promotes the circular economy by transforming plastic waste into a valuable resource for producing clean water and provides deeper insight into the optimization of the operating parameters using statistical tools.

title: AI Self-Efficacy and Transformational Leadership on Innovative Work Behavior: The Mediating Role of Work Engagement Among Jakarta Hotel Employees
abstractText: Background: Amid ongoing technological change, the hospitality sector relies more on the innovative work behavior (IWB) of its employees to stay competitive; nevertheless, how AI self-efficacy, transformational leadership, and work engagement together drive innovation in this field remains scarcely documented. Objective: Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework, this research investigates how AI self-efficacy and transformational leadership influence IWB among staff of four- and five-star hotels in Jakarta, treating work engagement as the mediating variable. Methods: A cross-sectional quantitative survey gathered responses from 180 hotel employees recruited via non-probability snowball sampling. The data were obtained through an online questionnaire and examined with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in AMOS. Results: AI self-efficacy exerted significant positive influences on both IWB and work engagement, whereas transformational leadership shaped work engagement significantly yet showed no significant direct influence on IWB. Work engagement was a significant predictor of IWB and partially carried the AI self-efficacy-IWB link, while it fully carried the transformational leadership-IWB link. Conclusion: The results show that personal and job resources reach employee innovation along distinct routes. AI self-efficacy contributes that is at once direct and indirect by way of work engagement, while transformational leadership operates mainly through engagement. To foster innovative work behavior, hotel management is advised to combine the cultivation of AI capability, the practice of transformational leadership, and initiatives that build employee engagement.

title: A Cell Wall-Associated Extracellular Catalase, Po CAT2, Confers Thermotolerance in Pleurotus ostreatus
abstractText: Abstract Heat stress induces excessive extracellular H2O2 accumulation, compromising redox homeostasis and mushroom productivity. However, the role of extracellular catalases (CATs) in basidiomycetes remains poorly understood. Here, we identified PoCAT2, a cell wall-associated extracellular catalase in the basidiomycete Pleurotus ostreatus, whose secretion may involve a vesicle-mediated unconventional protein secretion pathway. Heat stress and exogenous H2O2 induced PoCAT2 expression and wall-associated catalase activity. Unlike intracellular PoCAT1, PoCAT2 overexpression increased catalase activity in both intracellular and cell wall compartments, enhancing in situ H2O2 scavenging and promoting mycelial growth under both optimal and elevated temperatures. Moreover, PoCAT2 overexpression accelerated fruiting and increased mushroom yield. These findings establish PoCAT2 as an extracellular antioxidant component that contributes to thermotolerance and fruiting performance in P. ostreatus, providing a potential strategy for improving thermotolerance in cultivated mushrooms.

title: Improving asthma care: a call for leadership in health, equity and climate
abstractText: Now is the time for a co-ordinated revolution in asthma care in Aotearoa New Zealand. New Zealand can and should accelerate uptake of guideline-based single maintenance and reliever therapy and actively reduce the unnecessary use of therapies based only on short-acting beta agonists. These two actions together will achieve three important goals: reduced avoidable asthma harm, reduced health inequity and reduced healthcare greenhouse gas emissions. Leadership is required from clinicians, manufacturers, policymakers, funders and Pharmac.

title: PCR hyper-automation: an example of spinal muscular atrophy and severe combined immunodeficiency screening
abstractText: Abstract Objectives Most newborn bloodspot screening (NBS) programs use manual or semi-automated systems for severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) and spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) screening. We aimed to implement a hyper-automated, reliable, and greener system for large-scale SMA and SCID screening. Methods Single 3.2 mm punches from dried bloodspots (DBS) of controls and patients were punched into a 96-well plate. Up to four plates were loaded simultaneously onto an interfaced system comprising a Biomek-i7 for DNA extraction, an Echo-525 liquid handler for preparing a miniaturised master mix using acoustic energy in a 384-well plate, and a Quantstudio7-Flex qPCR instrument. The Eonis SMA-SCID kit was used to determine T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) semi-quantitatively and qualitatively detect deletion of exon 7 of the survival motor neuron1 gene ( SMN1 ). The AGREE calculator provided the analytical greenness score and EQA was used for ongoing independent assessment of performance. Results The system provided a turnaround time of less than 3 h for 384 DBS samples. The Echo-525 reduced the primer use by half compared to the manual process. The automated system improved the AGREE score compared to a manual process; 0.8 vs. 0.57 out of 1.0 respectively. Since its introduction in May 2023, and up to May 2026, EQA results have consistently demonstrated satisfactory performance using this automated workflow. Conclusions The study indicates the efficiency of this system as a first-tier NBS assay enabling the early, pre-symptomatic detection of SMA and SCID. This open system can potentially be applied to hyper-automate other large scale qPCR screening tests.

title: Fabrication, Transportation, and Installation of Fixed and Floating Offshore Wind Turbines: A State of the Art Review
abstractText: The rapid growth of offshore wind energy has increased the size and complexity of Offshore Wind Turbines (OWTs), making fabrication, transportation, and installation critical to project cost and schedule. However, previous studies have mostly examined these phases separately. This study presents a PRISMA-based Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of 49 peer-reviewed studies to identify key trends, challenges, and optimization opportunities in OWT construction. The review covers fixed and floating foundations, specialized installation vessels, and turbine pre-assembly strategies. Key quantitative findings reveal that weather windows vary significantly across foundation types: Tension Leg Platforms (TLPs) are limited to only 30–50% operational availability due to their high sensitivity (Hs < 0.8 m), while semi-submersibles achieve 70–85% availability with tolerance up to Hs < 2.0 m. Additionally, WTIVs capable of handling 15–20 MW turbines are projected to number only 8–10 vessels globally in 2025, creating a severe supply-demand gap that could drive day rates up by 50–100% by 2028. The findings demonstrate that construction efficiency depends on selecting methods suited to site conditions, vessel availability, technological limits, and logistical requirements. This review supports the development of safer, more efficient, and sustainable offshore wind construction practices.

title: The impact of surgical timing on functional improvement after arthroscopic repair of traumatic, full-thickness rotator cuff tears: is escalated care appropriate?
abstractText: aim: We aimed to assess whether surgical timing relative to a 120-day threshold influences functional improvement following arthroscopic repair of traumatic, full-thickness rotator cuff tears. methods: The clinical records of consecutive patients undergoing primary arthroscopic repair of a traumatic, full-thickness rotator cuff tear by a single fellowship-trained shoulder surgeon between August 2016 and April 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients without a confirmed traumatic injury mechanism, those with incomplete records and those with less than 12 months of post-operative follow-up were excluded. Eligible patients were allocated into an early group (surgery ≤120 days from injury, n=28) and a late group (surgery >120 days, n=50). The primary outcome was post-operative change in Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS). results: There were no significant differences between the groups in baseline demographic or surgical characteristics (all p>0.05). The early group had a significantly lower pre-operative OSS than the late group (mean 21.8 vs 27.5; p=0.012); however, post-operative OSS was not significantly different between groups (mean 46.4 vs 43.6; p=0.063). The early group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in OSS (mean +24.6 vs +16.1 points; p<0.001). On multivariate analysis, time from injury to surgery was an independent predictor of post-operative change in OSS (p<0.001). No significant between-group differences were identified for pain visual analogue scale (VAS), EQ-5D VAS or EQ-5D index. conclusion: Arthroscopic repair of traumatic, full-thickness rotator cuff tears within 120 days of injury is associated with significantly greater improvement in shoulder-specific function compared with delayed repair. These results support the introduction of escalated care pathways to facilitate timely surgical access for patients sustaining traumatic rotator cuff tears.

title: Implementation of The Guided Reading Learning Model To Improve Short Story Reading Skills In Students Kelas IV SD Negeri Lahendong
abstractText: This study aims to improve short story reading skills through the application of the Guided Reading learning model in fourth-grade students of Lahendong State Elementary School. The method used in this study is Classroom Action Research (CAR) which is implemented in two cycles. Each cycle consists of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. The research subjects were 13 fourth-grade students of Lahendong State Elementary School. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation and learning outcome tests. Data were analyzed using quantitative and qualitative descriptive analysis techniques. The results of the study indicate that the application of the Guided Reading learning model can improve students' short story reading skills. In cycle I, the average student learning outcomes reached 71.15% with a classical completion rate of 61.53%. After improvements were made in cycle II, the average student learning outcomes increased to 85.76% with a classical completion rate of 84.61%. These results indicate that students' short story reading skills have improved and have exceeded the established KKTP, which is 75%. Based on the research results, it can be concluded that the application of the Guided Reading learning model can improve the short story reading skills of fourth grade students at Lahendong State Elementary School.

Generation and Reconstruction of large-amplitude Cat States Based on Squeezed Magnon-Qubit hybrid systems
abstractText: Abstract As a bridge connecting different quantum systems, magnons have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in coherent coupling with various quantum systems such as photons, phonons, and qubits. As a result, hybrid systems composed of magnons have made significant progress in quantum technologies, quantum networks, and the construction of resource quantum states. Cat states, especially large-amplitude cat states, as a kind of important resource states, are not only important tools for testing quantum theory but also a cornerstone in the construction of logical qubits. However, large cat states in magnon systems are still challenging to prepare. A possible solution can be quantum state reconstruction using neural networks, which can partially transform the challenges in manipulating quantum systems into routine tasks in machine learning. We investigate a hybrid system consisting of squeezed magnons and superconducting flux qubits. This system enables enhanced generation of large Schrodinger cat states. Furthermore, we propose a method using neural ff network-based quantum state reconstruction to address two adverse factors: dissipation in magnon cat states and noise generated during measurements. Our research provides a feasible scheme for the preparation of large-amplitude cat states and offers viable approaches for the acquisition and error correction of quantum information in magnon cat states.

title: Synthesis of new thioxoimidazolidine containing azide moiety derived from acetophenone catalyzed by CdO nanoparticles and study of their biological effect
abstractText: The co-precipitation approach was used in this work to create cadmium oxide nanoparticles (CdO NPs) from cadmium nitrate. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used to assess the size and shape of the produced CdO NPs. As thioimidazolidine derivatives, new heterocyclic compounds with azide groups were created. Schiff bases were initially prepared using p-nitro, p-chloro, and p-bromo benzaldehydes with CdO. NPs as a catalyst. Filtration was used to successfully recover the catalyst. The target compounds (4a–c) were obtained by reacting these intermediates with ethyl chloroacetate, chloroacetyl chloride, and sodium azide. Spectroscopic methods such as FT-IR, ¹H-NMR, and ¹³C-NMR were used to characterize the produced compounds. The spectral analyses indicated that the synthesized compounds were obtained in a pure form, as no significant impurity signals were observed. Characteristic absorption bands were visible in the FT-IR spectra, especially for the azide group (N₃) at about 2115 cm⁻¹. Additionally, the synthetic substances' biological activity were assessed. Preliminary data on their safety profile was obtained by estimating acute toxicity by computing LD50 values. Strong broad-spectrum antibacterial activity was shown by the compounds against both Gram-negative bacteria like Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. and Gram-positive bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis. Additionally, encouraging antifungal efficacy against the pathogenic yeast Candida albicans was noted.

title: Lipton’s Journal
abstractText: Norman Mailer kept a journal of self-analysis for approximately four months in the mid-`1950s. This record was called the Lipton’s Journal. It took a Jungian approach to analyze Mailer’s life and work and the ways in which they might be modified. Further, it records his discovery of jazz as an important pathway to artistic renewal. Mailer’s self-analysis through Lipton’s Journal was transformational and foundational and it would become the key to all his future work, beginning in the 1960s. Reading the journal, we witness both the how and the why of Mailer’s personal transformation.

title: Synthesis and characterization of azo polymers based on chitosan and acrylamide derivatives
abstractText: Two azo-containing materials, an acrylamide-derived azo compound (AZO 1) and a chitosan-derived azo material (AZO-chitosan 2), were prepared by diazo coupling with o-cresol under alkaline conditions at 0–5 °C. The acrylamide-derived monomer was subsequently converted to an azo polymer by free-radical photopolymerization under nitrogen using 1-hydroxycyclohexyl phenyl ketone (Irgacure 184) as the photoinitiator. The products were characterized by FTIR, ¹H NMR, and ¹³C NMR spectroscopy, and their thermal behavior was evaluated by TGA and DSC. The acrylamide-derived azo compound was obtained in 78% yield, whereas the AZO-chitosan product was obtained in 70% yield. The spectral changes support formation of the azo-containing products and consumption of the polymerizable double bond. The two polymer samples showed TGA onset temperatures of 110 and 100 °C, 50% mass-loss temperatures of 260 and 270 °C, and residues of 92% and 90% at 600 °C, respectively. DSC gave glass-transition temperatures of 180 and 250 °C. These results establish the structural and preliminary thermal characteristics of the prepared materials. Molecular-weight distribution and photoisomerization were not measured and therefore remain subjects for further study.

title: Hyponatremia and Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Children with Type 1 Diabetes at an Indonesian Referral Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Background: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is the leading acute cause of death in children with type 1 diabetes. Indonesian data on its severity and biochemical profile are scarce. Objective: To examine whether admission sodium, potassium and urine ketone status are associated with severe DKA. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included children aged 1–18 years admitted in DKA (International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes 2022 criteria) to a tertiary hospital in Bali in 2022–2024. Hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L), hypokalemia (<3.5 mmol/L) and urine ketone 3+ were compared between severe and mild–moderate DKA with exact tests and Firth-penalized logistic regression across all joint tables compatible with the observed pairwise counts. Results: Of 54 children (mean age 11.22 years; 74.1% girls), 37 (68.5%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 55.3–79.3) had severe DKA. Hyponatremia occurred in 24 of 37 children with severe DKA (64.9%) and 4 of 17 with mild–moderate DKA (23.5%) (odds ratio 6.00, 95% CI 1.62–22.20; Fisher p = 0.008; Holm-adjusted p = 0.023). In Model 1, the adjusted odds ratio for hyponatremia ranged from 4.83 to 4.90 and was significant in every admissible joint table. Hypokalemia (53.7%; odds ratio 1.05, p = 1.000) and urine ketone 3+ (57.4%; odds ratio 1.85, p = 0.379) were not associated with severity. Conclusion: Two-thirds of children admitted in DKA to this Indonesian referral hospital had severe acidosis. Measured hyponatremia at admission was associated with severe DKA. It should prompt calculation of the glucose-corrected sodium. Potassium and dipstick ketone grade were not associated with severity.

The gender data gap in women’s cardiovascular health research in Aotearoa New Zealand: a call to action
abstractText: Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of mortality among women in Aotearoa New Zealand, yet significant gaps persist in our understanding of how heart disease uniquely affects women. A systematic review of women’s cardiovascular health in Aotearoa New Zealand revealed a concerning pattern: not a lack of cardiovascular research, but a persistent failure to adequately examine, report and analyse gender-specific data. Most studies provided minimal gender analysis beyond demographic representation, and many documented that women receive less treatment than men without exploring why these disparities exist or their clinical implications. This “gender data gap” mirrors international patterns of women’s under-representation in cardiovascular research and widespread underdiagnosis and undertreatment. The consequences are profound: clinical guidelines fail to address women’s cardiovascular presentations, systemic barriers remain invisible and healthcare providers lack the evidence base for gender-responsive care. For Māori and Pacific women, inadequate gender analysis compounds intersecting inequities. We present actionable recommendations for researchers, funders and publishers, including appropriate sample sizing for equal explanatory power, mandatory sex-disaggregated reporting, culturally responsive research practices and interrogation of observed gender differences. Closing the gender data gap is essential for health equity and justice for all Aotearoa New Zealand women.

title: Trap-Assisted Photoconductive Gain and Wavelength-Dependent Response of Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Heterojunction Ultraviolet Detectors
abstractText: Abstract Ultraviolet photodetection is essential for secure optical communication, environmental monitoring and early warning systems, yet conventional GaN-based Schottky detectors rely on evaporated metal electrodes that introduce interfacial defects and limited UV transmittance. Here we report a solution-processed Ti 3 C 2 F MXene/GaN van der Waals Schottky heterojunction UV photodetector formed by low-temperature drop-coating. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Raman analysis confirm the surface termination and structural integrity of the transferred MXene, and density-functional-theory calculations rationalize the tunable Schottky barrier. The device exhibits a low dark current of ~74 nA near zero bias, about 30% lower than that of conventional Ti/Au Schottky GaN detectors. Wavelength-resolved measurements at 300, 310 and 320 nm show a photocurrent ordering of 320 nm > 310 nm > 300 nm, governed by the interplay between photon penetration depth and near-surface recombination. Under 320 nm illumination at 1.91 W/cm 2 and -4 V, a responsivity of 0.58 A/W, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 212% and a specific detectivity of 3.35 × 10 11 Jones are obtained; the above-unity EQE indicates trap-mediated internal photoconductive gain in GaN. Periodic UV switching yields rise/fall times of 1.22/0.80 s with an on/off ratio of ~2.2 and <5% peak-to-peak variation over four cycles. These results establish MXene/GaN van der Waals heterojunctions as a low-cost, solution-processable platform for wavelength-resolved UV detection.

Evaluasi Aplikasi Manajemen Persuratan Berbasis Web pada Cabang Dinas Kehutanan Wilayah Kabupaten Sumenep
abstractText: Correspondence management at the Sumenep Regency Forestry Service Branch faces scattered archives, remote approval constraints, and incomplete disposition records. Application support for process traceability and user experience across four service areas has not been evaluated jointly. This study offers a contextual contribution by combining assessments of archives, role-based authorization, dispositions, and user experience within internal correspondence management. It evaluates a web-based application and identifies improvements. An evaluative qualitative descriptive method employed observations, informal interviews, document reviews, and technical inspections, complemented by the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ). Operational evidence covered May–September 2026, with January–April records providing available comparisons. The October 12, 2026 survey involved 11 users excluding the author: four managerial officials and seven staff members. The application provides digital archives, hierarchical approvals, dispositions, and assignment letters. One outgoing letter required 39 minutes from submission to finalization; recovery testing succeeded within its scope. All six UEQ scales scored 2.32–2.59 and achieved Excellent benchmark ratings. Findings indicate support for correspondence traceability and positive user perceptions; however, performance improvements cannot be quantified without comparable baseline measurements. Form protection, PDF processing, and backup procedures require strengthening. Implementation supports SDG 16, Target 16.6, through documented authority and traceable administrative processes at the work unit level.
